## 2026-07-21 | Worker (scheduled burst) | conductor/rotation-selection | pattern

**Decision:** self-caught and reverted before any PR opened — no code/doc change merged.

**Failure category:** actionable (a real gap in the ad-hoc selection script, not environment noise)

**Subject:** A manual ready-task scan across all projects built the active-project set from
`project-overrides.yaml` but never actually filtered the priority-order walk by it, so a
**retired** project's `ready` task (`animation-studio/t-001`) surfaced as pickable and got
claimed and worked (RESEARCH.md drafted, TALKBACK entry written) before the mistake was
caught — `project-overrides.yaml` marks `animation-studio: status: retired` (2026-07-19,
conductor/t-039), superseded by `animation-manager`, which already did the equivalent
research/pitch-queue tasks.

**Detail:**
- This session's goal was explicit project *rotation* (not just `next_ready_task.py`'s
  highest-priority pick, which would have deterministically re-picked `ai-art-academy/t-010`
  — already fully cycled ~30min earlier this same hour). That meant hand-rolling a
  full-portfolio ready-task scan instead of using the vetted `next_ready_task.py`/
  `claim_task.py` pipeline's own active-project filtering for the *selection* step (claiming
  itself still went through `claim_task.py`, which is why this was caught: the retraction
  had to be written by hand since there's no "release claim" helper).
- Root cause: wrote `active = {o['slug'] for o in overrides if o.get('status')=='active'}`
  but then iterated `for proj in priority: ...` without an `if proj not in active: continue`
  guard — the variable was computed and silently unused.
- Caught only because `python scripts/audit_roadmaps.py`'s diff (run before committing, as
  routine verification) showed `animation-studio` as `retired` in its project-inventory
  table — worth noting that `audit_roadmaps.py`'s own project-inventory table is actually a
  faster active/retired sanity check than re-deriving the set by hand.

**Suggested action:** a future ad-hoc rotation-style scan should either (a) reuse
`next_ready_task.py`'s own active-project filtering logic instead of re-deriving it inline,
or (b) run `python scripts/audit_roadmaps.py` — or at minimum grep
`project-overrides.yaml` for the specific candidate project's `status:` line — as the very
last check immediately before `claim_task.py`, not just as part of an earlier broad sweep.
`claim_task.py` itself has no independent active/retired check (it only guards against
double-claiming a task), so it will happily claim a task on a retired project if asked to.

**Kaizen task:** none filed as a roadmap task — the fix is a scan-methodology lesson, not a
code gap; recorded here and in `LEARNING.yaml` instead.

  wrap-up commit had already landed.

  had already changed the same `roadmap.yaml` lines minutes earlier. Diagnosed via `git fetch
  origin main` + `git diff`, confirmed #1010's diff was functionally identical intent (same
  task, same PR #850 reference, same session id in the note), then reconciled by hard-resetting
  the local branch onto `origin/main` and re-applying only the net-new part (the TALKBACK.md

  force-pushing over #1010's already-merged content or leaving both duplicate notes on the task.

**Suggested action:** When a session resumes an in-progress claim it doesn't fully remember
(stale-looking `status: claimed` plus a live open PR that already matches the task), check
`git log`/recent merged PRs for that project/task-id *before* writing a new wrap-up commit —
not just before touching the implementation. The implementation-reuse check (open-PR lookup)
already happened correctly here; the gap was not re-running the equivalent check for the
roadmap/TALKBACK log commit that normally follows a merge. Worth a line in AGENTS.md's
"Rotation collisions" section generalizing it beyond concurrent-session collisions to
same-session post-compaction collisions, since the failure mode and the fix (fetch origin
before writing, reconcile via diff rather than blind force-push) are identical either way.

**Kaizen task:** none filed this cycle — logging the pattern here is the intended first step;
if this recurs, promote it to an AGENTS.md addition rather than a repeated TALKBACK note.

## 2026-07-25 | Reviewer (scheduled agent run) | ci-janitor todos #751/#752 + model-builder/t-029 | pattern

**Decision:** merged kind_robots PR #953 (facet-catalog seed perf fix) and PR #954 (model-builder keyboard-accessible matrix rows).

**Failure category:** null — both PRs were already implemented and CI-green by the time this cycle picked them up; reviewed and merged rather than reimplemented.

**Subject:** Session-start sweep found two open kind_robots PRs against ci-janitor todos #751 (created 14:05) and #752 (created 15:31), both "Fix red CI: Kind Robots Cypress Tests," same underlying root cause on two different commits. PR #953 (branch `claude/dazzling-ptolemy-7ed1le`) was already up with a real fix; reviewed and merged it instead of duplicating work.

**Detail:**
- Root cause per PR #953's own diagnosis: `seedFacetCatalog.ts` ran a `findUnique` per candidate/alias (~1300 candidates) and per character field-value serially against a ProxySQL connection with pipelining disabled — several thousand serial WAN round trips on every production build, blowing Vercel's max build time (`BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME`). Cypress CI on `main` was red only because it could never find a live deploy of the target commit, not because of a test regression.
- Fix preloads existing Facet/FacetAlias/CharacterFacet state once (two queries) into shared Maps, then spreads independent writes across the connection pool (`WRITE_CONCURRENCY=8`, within `DEFAULT_CONNECTION_LIMIT=10`) instead of awaiting them serially. Verified before merging: candidates are already deduped upstream by `normalizeFacetLookupKey(title)` in the `candidates` Map (line ~195), and `slugify` is a strictly coarser normalization of the same alnum-run sequence — so two catalog entries with distinct keys cannot collide on `slug`, which rules out the unique-constraint race that concurrent writes would otherwise risk. The only real behavior change is alias tie-breaking: when two distinct facets legitimately share a candidate alias, the old serial code deterministically gave it to whichever candidate ran first in array order; under concurrency it's now a nondeterministic race between whichever `upsert` lands last. Low-impact (no crash, no data loss, just possible alias reassignment in a rare contested-alias case) — not worth blocking the merge over, since the current state (every build broken) is strictly worse.
- Checks were green on both PRs (TypeScript/Contract verifiers/facet-catalog/GitGuardian on #953; same plus `verify` on #954) but neither PR includes the `Kind Robots Cypress Tests` workflow itself — that only runs against `main` post-deploy, so the real verification is the next production build after this merge. Flagging for whoever next touches this: watch the next `vercel-build` log and the next Cypress run on `main` before marking todos #751/#752 done — CI-JANITOR.md's own policy says only complete a todo after verification passes, and this session couldn't run the seed end-to-end against a live DB in-sandbox.
- PR #954 (model-builder/t-029, Worker branch `worker/model-builder-t-029-keyboard-matrix-6d91`) adds a real `<button>` inside the stage-matrix row's name cell with `aria-pressed`/`aria-label`/focus ring, keeping the existing whole-row click-to-select behavior via `@click.stop` on the new button plus the original `@click` on `<tr>`. Scoped one-file template change, 5/5 CI checks green. No concerns.

**What was good:**
- Both PRs' authors clearly named the root cause (not just symptoms) and cited git commit history / prior incident context (facet-catalog cutover date, exact build failure signature) rather than guessing.
- #953's own test-plan section was honest about the local-sandbox limitation (no live DB to run the seed end-to-end) instead of overclaiming verification.

**What to improve:**
- None specific this cycle — both were clean, well-scoped, well-tested-as-far-as-possible.

**Kaizen task:** none filed this cycle — the fix already addresses the systemic weakness (serial per-record DB round trips in seed/migration scripts under a no-pipelining ProxySQL connection); revisit only if another seed/migration script hits the same build-timeout pattern.

## 2026-07-25 | Reviewer (scheduled burst-mode agent run) | ci-janitor todo #751/#752 | pattern

**Decision:** merged kind_robots PR #955 (own fix, no Worker involved this cycle).

**Failure category:** null — real production outage found, root-caused, and fixed; also caught a second, related bug live while verifying the first fix.

**Subject:** Todos (#751, #752, both HIGH, "Fix red CI: Kind Robots Cypress Tests") took priority over roadmap rotation per AGENTS.md step 0. Investigation found the Cypress CI redness was a symptom, not the disease: kind_robots production had been failing to deploy at all for 4.5+ hours (`BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME` on 6 consecutive production builds since commit `3b69cff`), so the Cypress workflow's "wait for deploy" step was timing out waiting for a deploy that would never land.

**Detail:**
- Root cause: the same-day "Make Facets the canonical creative catalog" cutover (`7c47da2`) added `utils/scripts/seedFacetCatalog.ts`, run unconditionally on every production build via `scripts/vercel-build.mjs`. It re-read the DB with a `findUnique` per candidate/alias/character-field (~1300 catalog candidates + a full `Character` table backfill, several thousand serial WAN round trips against a ProxySQL host with pipelining disabled) — enough to blow Vercel's build time ceiling on every single deploy since.
- By the time I'd diagnosed this and was about to write a fix, another session/agent had already landed and merged kind_robots PR #953 (`fix(facet-catalog): stop production builds timing out during seed`) — same root cause, same fix shape (preload state once instead of per-record reads, spread writes across the connection pool). Verified rather than duplicated: watched `#953`'s production deploy go READY (~14.5min build, vs. the prior 45min+ timeouts) via the Vercel MCP connector.
- While that deploy was finishing, a second production build (`#954`, pushed ~2s after `#953`) started concurrently and got stuck — caught this live rather than assuming green. Root cause: `seedFacetCatalog.ts`'s create-vs-update branch decides per-run from its own up-front snapshot, so two concurrent seed runs can both see the same slug as "new" and both call `facet.create()`; the loser hit a `Facet_slug_key` unique-constraint violation (P2002). Worse, that per-item throw escaped `runWithConcurrency`'s `Promise.all` (which rejects the instant the *first* lane throws) while the other 7 lanes kept running against the same Prisma client — `main()`'s `finally` then disconnected that client while those lanes were still mid-query, hanging them forever and silently reintroducing `BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME` all over again (confirmed stuck 45+min with no further build log output).
- Fixed and merged kind_robots PR #955: (1) `runWithConcurrency` now catches per-item inside each lane and aggregates errors, so every lane fully drains before the shared client disconnects; (2) the facet-create path (`createOrRecoverFacet`) catches P2002 and recovers by reading the race winner's row and updating it instead of failing/hanging the whole seed. Verified `tsc --noEmit` / `eslint` / `prettier --check` locally (provisioned via `provision_kind_robots_deps.sh`), then confirmed on the real PR: TypeScript, Contract verifiers, facet-catalog, and GitGuardian checks all green; merged squash `9be40e8`. Watched that deploy go READY cleanly (~12.3min) and manually triggered `cypress.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` (it's schedule-triggered, not push-triggered, per its own header comment) to confirm green rather than waiting up to 30min for the next scheduled run.
- Completed both Todos (`complete_todo.py 751`, `752`) once production was confirmed healthy on the fixed commit.

**What was good:**
- Didn't stop at "someone else already fixed it" — actually watched the fix deploy through to READY instead of assuming a merged PR meant the incident was over. That's what caught the second, genuinely new concurrent-seed-race bug before it could cause another silent outage.

**What to improve:**
- None specific — this was reactive incident response on infrastructure code outside any project roadmap, not a roadmap task's checklist to improve.

**Kaizen task:** none filed — this fix already targets the exact systemic weakness (concurrent-write safety in one-time backfill scripts run from build hooks); no roadmap project owns `utils/scripts/seedFacetCatalog.ts` to attach a kaizen task to. Worth remembering generically: any script invoked from `vercel-build.mjs` can run concurrently across back-to-back production deploys (a common conductor pattern when several PRs merge in quick succession) and must be safe under that, not just under repeated-but-serial invocation.

Both are legitimate, unrelated, reversible follow-up tasks that happened to grab the same next-available id from two branches that forked before either saw the other's addition. First resolution pass (pushed ~04:12 UTC) kept PR #1095's task as `t-028` and renumbered `main`'s to `t-029` — but before that landed, a live concurrent session claimed and started *implementing* `digital-storefront/t-028` (the swag-rail task, matching `main`'s original numbering) — see commits `857530b`/`2d1fdd3` (status claimed → review, kind_robots PR #995 opened) — with its own session id, commit messages, and the kind_robots PR itself all keying on `t-028`. Renumbering that task out from under live in-progress work would have orphaned those external references. Re-resolved (second pass): reverted the swag-rail task back to `t-028` with `main`'s live content (claimed_by/PR #995 note) fully intact and untouched, and renumbered PR #1095's own task (`Resource.commercialSafe` gate) to `t-029` instead — it has no external references yet, so it was the safe one to move.

**Suggested action / kaizen note:** two sessions filing a kaizen task from the *same* Reviewer-merge event (kind-robots/t-045 and t-047 both landed close together) independently computed "next free id" from a `main` that hadn't yet seen the other's addition, and a third session then started live-implementing one of the colliding ids before the conflict was even resolved. Worth considering whether `claim_task.py`-style atomic ID reservation (already used for task *claims*) should extend to new-task-id assignment for Reviewer-authored kaizen tasks, to close this same race for task creation, not just task claiming. When resolving a same-id collision, prefer keeping whichever side already has live external references (an open PR, a claim, a session id baked into commit messages) under its current id, and renumber the side with no external references yet — check for exactly this before assuming the earlier of two resolutions is still correct, since `main` can keep moving between merge attempts. Not filing a new task for this myself this cycle — flagging here for whoever next touches `scripts/claim_task.py`/roadmap tooling to weigh in, since it's a tooling design question rather than a scoped bug fix.

narrow write-input type, `RewardFacetAssignment`, against a full Prisma row that carries
extra fields, causing TS2677/TS2322). Diagnosed the exact root cause via a subagent
(checked out the branch locally, ran the real `npm run test`/vue-tsc command instead of
guessing from the truncated CI log), then wrote and pushed a fix
(`server/utils/rewardFacetCatalog.ts`, commit `1f17023`: introduced a separate
`RewardFacetRecord` type via `Prisma.RewardFacetGetPayload`, matching the existing
`RawFacet` pattern in `facetCatalog.ts`, rather than widening the shared write-input
type also used by `facets.put.ts`).

**Detail — the race:** by the time the push landed, the PR had already been merged
(`merged_by: silasfelinus`, squash commit `8dadfb1`) using an *earlier* version of the
branch — a different, independently-written fix for the identical bug (an explicit
`for`/`continue`/`push` loop building the assignments array by named field, avoiding the
type-predicate narrowing entirely, rather than my `Prisma.RewardFacetGetPayload`
approach). My pushed commit was never included in the merge and is now orphaned on the
still-open branch `agent/daily-dream-facet-blueprints-v2` (session credentials 403 on
`git push --delete`; no branch-janitor workflow exists in kind_robots to force-delete it
the way conductor's does — left as harmless clutter, flagged here rather than silently
dropped).

  the new `main`, regenerated the Prisma client, and ran the actual `npm run test`
  (vue-tsc) locally — clean, 0 errors. The concurrent fix is correct; no follow-up work
  needed on `main` itself.

**Suggested action:** this is the same "two sessions converge on the same fix from
different starting points" race already documented for roadmap-task claims
(`claim_task.py`) and new-task-id assignment (2026-07-26 `digital-storefront/t-028`
entry above) — just now observed on a PR-fix-push instead. No tooling gap to close here
specifically (a squash-merge race on someone else's live PR isn't something a Reviewer
session claiming/reviewing can lock against), but worth remembering: after pushing a fix
to any PR you don't own the merge button for, re-fetch and diff against the PR's actual
merged state before assuming your push is what shipped — do not extrapolate the fix's
presence from "I pushed it" alone.

(`conductor/t-080`, filed after finding a fresh cross-project ArtJob failure cluster —
`error: "ComfyUI reported a workflow error"` — spanning coloring-book, packmaker,
superkate-hairstyle-ai, and music-mentor). Re-checked `GET /api/art/queue/stats` before
touching anything: the cluster was still live and had grown to 13 occurrences, now also

**Detail:**
- Dispatched an Explore agent (kept out of main context) to trace where the exact string
  gets set. It found the string lives in *this* repo, not kind_robots:
  `ops/home-server/relay_agent.py`'s `run_comfy()` and `relay_media_agent.py`'s duplicate
  `run_comfy_with_recovery()` both poll ComfyUI's `GET /history/{prompt_id}`, see
  `status.status_str == "error"`, and raise a hardcoded generic string — never inspecting
  `status.messages`, which is where ComfyUI's own `execution_error` tuple (node id, node
  type, exception message, traceback) actually lives. The detail is discarded permanently:
  not logged, not stored, not forwarded to kind_robots' `ArtJob.error` column, which just
  gets the generic string verbatim.

  of the 13 already-failed jobs — the ComfyUI history entries are transient and the detail
  was never captured. Treated the diagnostic gap itself as the fixable, in-scope part of
  an "investigate" task: added `describe_comfy_error(entry)` to `relay_agent.py` (parses
  `status.messages` for an `execution_error` entry, formats `"node {id} ({type}):
  {exception_message}"`) and wired it into both call sites' error branch.
- Added 4 tests (`tests/test_relay_completion_provenance.py`): the helper directly (hit
  and miss cases) plus both `run_comfy()` and `run_comfy_with_recovery()` end-to-end,
  asserting the raised `RuntimeError` carries the real node/exception text. Ran the full
  suite locally before opening the PR (542 passed, 1 skipped, pytest/pyyaml installed
  fresh in-sandbox since neither was preinstalled) rather than relying on CI alone as the
  first signal.
- Did not attempt to guess or fix the underlying ComfyUI failure cause itself — no access
  to the home-relay/ComfyUI logs from this sandbox, and guessing at a workflow-graph bug
  without the actual exception text would be exactly the kind of unverified fix this repo's
  rules warn against. Documented that explicitly in both the PR body and the task note so
  the next session doesn't mistake "diagnostic gap fixed" for "root cause fixed."

**What was good:**
- Recognized that a generic, identically-worded error across unrelated projects was more
  likely a reporting-code blind spot than four independent product bugs, and verified that
  hypothesis by reading the actual relay source rather than guessing from the ArtJob error
  text alone.
- Didn't overstate the fix's scope — the PR body, roadmap note, and this entry all say
  plainly that the underlying cause is still unknown and won't be knowable until a future
  failure lands with the new detail.

**Kaizen task:** none filed as a new task — the roadmap note itself already carries the
follow-up instruction (re-check `queue/stats`' `recentFailed` in a few cycles for an entry
with real node/exception detail, and root-cause from there). Filing a separate task now
would just duplicate that note with no new information to act on yet.

  session hadn't seen the auto-queued event land yet) and pushed that directly to
  `main`, bumping the task's `updated` timestamp.
- My manual `updated` timestamp landed *after* the queued event's own `updated`.
  `process_task_events.py`'s `stale_reason()` compares the two and, since roadmap
  timestamps only move forward, would have permanently treated the event as stale
  on its next run -- silently `unlink()`ing it, discarding its `learning:` payload
  with no error and no trace, per `process()`'s early-return path (conductor/t-085,
  discovered same-session, `scripts/process_task_events.py` lines ~311-320).
- Caught it only because I happened to `git fetch` and notice the queued event file
  still sitting in `task-events/` before the next processor run consumed it.
  Recovered by hand: appended the event's exact `learning` text to `LEARNING.yaml`
  via the new `append_ledger_entry.py` (this same cycle's t-085 deliverable), then
  removed the now-permanently-stale event file with an explanatory commit.

**Suggested action:** filed conductor/t-086 (kaizen) -- when a Worker session
manually closes a task that the PR-merge auto-queue mechanism might *also* be about
to (or has already) queued a completion event for, check `task-events/` for a
matching `project`/`task` file BEFORE hand-writing the `status: done` transition,
and either let the queued event apply on its own (if its `learning`/`note` payload
is already correct) or explicitly consume it (apply its payload, then delete it)
rather than racing it blind. The general pattern: any two independent writers that
both derive "is this stale" from a monotonic timestamp need to check each other's
state before writing, not just their own.

## 2026-07-27 | Reviewer (conductor burst-mode session) | conductor | pattern
type: pattern

**Subject:** A third variant of the concurrent-write race family: two independent sessions both resolving a merge conflict on the *same* open PR at the same time, where the losing resolution can silently regress already-merged canonical content.

**Detail:**
- PR #1197 (music-mentor/t-007 close-out) and PR #1195 (ai-art-academy/t-010, which had accidentally bundled a duplicate music-mentor/t-007 close-out alongside its real scope) both touched `projects/music-mentor/roadmap.yaml`, `projects/music-mentor/TALKBACK.md`, and `LEARNING.yaml`.

- The push was rejected (plain non-fast-forward, no force used) — a second, independent session had pushed its own conflict-resolution commit to the same PR #1195 branch in the meantime, but that commit took the wrong approach: it re-merged `main` while keeping #1195's *stale* copy of the music-mentor content, which would have silently reverted #1197's already-merged, more-complete version had it landed first.
- Recovered by fetching the branch's new tip, merging it in (not overwriting it), and re-resolving in favor of `main`'s canonical content again. Verified with `git diff origin/main --stat` before the final push that the PR's diff was exactly its intended scope (33 insertions/16 deletions, ai-art-academy files only) — no residual music-mentor changes.
- Documented the general pattern and recovery procedure in `AGENTS.md` under "Concurrent PR-conflict-resolution races" (sibling section to the existing "Rotation collisions" / "Same-session post-compaction collisions").

**Suggested action:** No tooling gap here — the safety net (git's ordinary non-fast-forward push rejection) worked exactly as it should and is what caught this. The gap was purely that the pattern and its correct recovery weren't written down anywhere, so a session hitting it had to re-derive the right approach from first principles. That's now fixed in AGENTS.md. Filed no new task — the AGENTS.md edit landed in the same PR as this note.

pipeline (`scripts/consume_art_requests.py` / `scripts/distribute_images.py`) that had
silently blocked art generation for ~15 active projects for weeks. See conductor#1380
and #1381 for the fixes/recovery.

**Finding 1 — weak-prompt gate blocked every pending request.** `consume_art_requests.py`'s
`weak_prompt_reason()` gate (added at some point after the original missing-image fallback
prompts were written) was correctly refusing to render the frozen generic template prompts
("flat minimal app icon for X, bold clean vector shapes...", "wide cinematic hero image for
X, expressive scene with clear atmosphere...") — but every one of the 37 pending requests in
`art-prompts.yaml` matched one of those templates, so **zero** art had generated through this
path in weeks regardless of relay health. This is the real explanation for why every
project's "Polish and upgrade front-end surface" task kept finding step (1) art blocked even
during sessions that confirmed the relay itself was up. Fixed by rewriting 21 of the 37 (the
project icon/hero ones) with concrete art direction; the remaining 16 `userupload-*` entries
need real captioning of the uploaded image content, not a template fix — left pending.

**Finding 2 — basename collision in the staging/lookup path.** Every kind_robots-target
project hero image uses the identical relative path convention
`public/images/projects/{slug}/hero.webp` — same basename ("hero.webp") for every project.
`consume_art_requests.py`'s `save_result()` stages generated images in `projects/process/`
keyed only by `Path(image_path).name`, so processing two such requests in the same run
silently overwrites the first project's generated image with the second's before either gets
distributed. `distribute_images.py`'s `build_lookup()` has the same basename-only-key
limitation on the read side. Caught this live (lost voice-lab's and humboldt-scoop's first
hero renders mid-batch) and recovered both from their still-live `ArtImage` records via
direct `GET /api/art/image/{id}` rather than losing them. Not fixed at the root this cycle —
flagging as a real kaizen candidate: `save_result`/`build_lookup` should key staging files by
`{slug}-{variant}` or similar, not bare basename, before the remaining 7 blocked kind_robots
hero entries (ruler-hooked, newsfeed, packmaker, challenge-center, davinci, media-watchlist,
coat-dance) can be safely batch-generated in one run.

**Suggested action:** a future cycle should either (a) add a small kaizen task to
`projects/conductor/roadmap.yaml` to fix `save_result`'s staging filename to include the
project slug (and update `build_lookup` to match), or (b) generate the remaining 7
kind_robots hero entries one at a time via `--id-prefix`, manually renaming the staged file
out of `projects/process/hero.webp` between each run, until the root fix lands.

## 2026-07-29 | Worker (conductor scheduled burst-mode rotation) | conductor (missing-image art pipeline) | response

**Subject:** Landed kaizen option (a) from the same-day "missing-image art pipeline" finding
above: fixed the basename-collision root cause instead of just filing a task for it.
See conductor/t-093.

**Detail:**
- `consume_art_queue_core.save_result()` and `distribute_images.build_lookup()` both keyed
  staged/looked-up files by `Path(image_path).name` alone. Every kind_robots hero request
  shares the literal basename "hero.webp" (slug only in the parent directory), so two
  requests in the same or even a later run silently clobbered each other -- and
  kind_robots-target files are retained indefinitely in `projects/process/`, so the
  collision persists across runs, not just within a batch.
- Added `staged_filename(entry)`: folds `project_slug`/`variant` into `{slug}-{variant}{suffix}`
  (matching the naming convention every other project icon/card/hero file already uses)
  only when those fields are present and the basename doesn't already encode the slug.
  No-op for every other pipeline (art-prompts `images:`/`inspirations:`, `art-generate.yaml`
  batch), confirmed by the full existing suite passing unchanged plus 4 new regression tests.
- Also fixed an unrelated, pre-existing `LEARNING.yaml` schema gap found while running the
  full suite (a `done` record missing `failure_category: null`) so `main`'s test suite is
  green again -- one line, confirmed pre-existing via `git stash` before touching anything.

**Suggested action:** the remaining 16 `userupload-*` weak-prompt entries from the same
finding still need real captioning, not a template fix -- left for a future cycle, matching
the original finding's note.

## 2026-07-29 | Worker (conductor scheduled cycle) | ai-art-academy/t-010 | pattern

**Subject:** `build_workspace.py`'s `request_is_complete()` conflated "generation succeeded" with "delivery confirmed" for kind_robots-target art-prompts.yaml requests, silently pruning the tracking record for a retained-but-undelivered file the moment its status flipped to `done`.

**Detail:**
- The 2026-07-28 `fauvism` style-preview thumbnail (ArtJob 2775/ArtImage 13125) was generated successfully but its relay delivery to `media.acrocatranch.com` apparently never completed. `consume_art_requests.py`'s `mark_done()` sets `status: done` immediately after generation regardless of delivery outcome, and `distribute_images.py` correctly RETAINed the file in `projects/process/` for later delivery -- but `request_is_complete()` (used by `prune_art_prompts()`) returned `True` the instant it saw `status: done`, so the very next `distribute_images.py` run where *any other file* moved silently dropped the fauvism request entry (commit `97f90d8`) while the render was still sitting undelivered. With no yaml record left to re-match against, the orphaned file then got swept into `projects/process/unmatched/` on the following run (`a84595c`).
- This is a second, independent trigger for the same class of data-loss bug the 2026-07-27 fix (never writing a local kind_robots checkout copy, see the docstring on `distribute_images.py`'s kind_robots branch) only partially closed -- that fix addressed *where* the file gets written; this bug was in how completeness is judged for pruning the *record*, a different code path entirely.
- Fixed in kind_robots-adjacent conductor PR #1397: `request_is_complete()` now also requires the staged local file to be gone before treating a kind_robots-target `done` request as complete. Added `tests/test_build_workspace.py` covering the fix and a control case for non-kind_robots requests (unaffected).
- Restored the fauvism request entry and its file (moved back from `unmatched/`); production is still 404 for it -- delivery itself is unresolved, just no longer silently untracked.

**Suggested action:** worth checking whether other consumers in the art pipeline make the same "status: done implies delivered" assumption for kind_robots-target work (e.g. project icon/card/hero requests, inspirations) -- this fix only covers the `requests:` section's `request_is_complete()` path. Also: there is currently no in-repo mechanism to retry delivery-only for an already-staged kind_robots render without discarding it and re-rendering from scratch; a future session with home-relay access should look at whether that gap is worth closing, or whether staged files are expected to eventually get picked up by an out-of-band relay process this repo doesn't otherwise track.

  ratio when milestones carry no signal (`if total_m and done_m > 0: ... ; if tasks:
  return done_t / len(tasks)`). kind_robots' `computeProgress` had only the
  milestone half. Agents close tasks reliably but almost never flip
  `milestone.status`, so any project whose milestones were all left `not-started`
  rendered as **0%** on the site while STATUS.md reported the truth.
- Measured across the whole registry: 16 of 43 wrong. Every flagship completion was
  affected — davinci, newsfeed, challenge-center, ecosystem-map, engagement and
  global-ui are all 100% by task count and all showed zero. conductor itself showed
  0% against a real 96.8%; media-watchlist 93.8%, humboldt-scoop-cms 91.7%,
  storymaker 90%. The other 27 matched to within rounding, which is presumably why
  this survived so long — the board looked plausible, not broken.
- Fixed in kind_robots `fa7db9c`: ported the fallback, extracted the roadmap parser
  and progress math into `server/utils/conductorRoadmap.ts`, and added
  `verifyConductorProgressParity.ts` — it asserts the endpoint's number against a
  direct transcription of build_status.py's formula, so the next time one side's
  formula moves, CI says which fixtures disagree instead of the board quietly
  drifting again.
- Two adjacent gaps found while measuring, both fixed here:
  `lora-ingestion` had a roadmap and appeared in STATUS.md but was never added to
  `project-overrides.yaml` — and the registry, not the `projects/` directory, is
  what defines projects for the front end, so it was invisible on the site and
  skipped by `sync_projects.py` entirely. And `build_conductor_summary.py`'s
  `fetch_roadmaps()` scanned `projects/*/roadmap.yaml` with no lifecycle
  cross-check, which is why retired `approval-portal` t-004/t-005 kept appearing
  under **ACTION NEEDED**. Adding the check drops 15 phantom needs-human gates and
  3 stale blocked tasks from the report.

**Suggested action:** the `build_conductor_summary.py` case is the third instance of
the same bug class — CLAUDE.md already documents it for the session-startup sweep
(2026-07-25, career-transition/pinball-hero), and it was independently present in
the automated summary builder. Worth auditing every remaining consumer of
`glob("projects/*/roadmap.yaml")` for a missing `project-overrides.yaml` join rather
than waiting to trip over the fourth. `scripts/build_status.py` is the obvious next
one to check — it counts 44 "active projects" including retired ones.

## 2026-07-31 | Reviewer → Worker | conductor | critique

**Subject:** Follow-up to the progress-parity entry above — the formula was the
smaller half. The front end's roadmap parser was mis-reading 30 of 44 roadmaps,
including conductor's own (26 of 95 tasks).

**Detail:**
- The first pass compared *formulas*: I ran both progress functions over
  PyYAML-parsed roadmaps and found 16 disagreements. That understated it, because
  it never exercised the front end's own parser. Re-running with the actual
  TypeScript `parseRoadmapYaml` over all 44 live roadmaps put the count at **30**.
- `parseRoadmapYaml` was a hand-rolled line-regex reader that understood exactly
  one spelling of YAML: two-space-indented block sequences, no blank lines between
  items, block scalars only. Conductor's roadmaps are written by hand, by `yq`, and
  by PyYAML dumps, so they use every legal spelling. It never threw — it returned
  partial data, which reads downstream as a smaller, less-complete project:
  `davinci` 1 of 4 milestones and 1 of 16 tasks (blank lines between items),
  `lora-ingestion` 0 of 6 (sequences at column 0), `challenge-center` 0 of 20 and
  `conductor` 26 of 95 (a double-quoted multi-line `notes_from_silas` that the
  reader fell into and never recovered from).
- Replaced with the `yaml` npm package. All 44 roadmaps now parse to identical
  milestone/task counts and identical progress against PyYAML + build_status.py.
- **Two of our roadmaps are not actually valid YAML.** `lora-ingestion` and
  `art-generator-connect` had `notes_from_silas` as a single-quoted flow scalar
  with continuation lines at column 0. The spec requires those to be indented
  deeper than the key; PyYAML accepts it anyway, a YAML 1.2 parser raises
  "Missing closing 'quote" and abandons the file. Every conductor-side tool uses
  PyYAML, so nothing here ever noticed — the front end just showed both projects
  as empty. Both repaired to block scalars, content preserved.
- Added `scripts/check_roadmap_yaml.py`, wired ahead of the audit step in
  `roadmap-audit.yml`. `audit_roadmaps.py` cannot catch this class by
  construction: it reads with the same permissive parser that creates it.

**Suggested action:** the real hazard is that `yaml.safe_dump` *produces* the
invalid shape whenever a value has long lines and a colon-space — which is exactly
what `notes_from_silas` looks like. Any script that round-trips a roadmap through
PyYAML can reintroduce it silently. The new check is a backstop, not a fix; the
better habit is `default_style='|'` (or `allow_unicode=True` plus a block-scalar
representer) on any dump that writes a roadmap back to disk. Worth checking every
script that calls `safe_dump` on a roadmap — `set_task_field.py` and `close_task.py`
are the high-traffic ones.

## 2026-07-31 | Worker | system | ci-janitor incident (kind_robots Todos #1003-#1006, #986)

type: pattern

**Subject:** Six consecutive scheduled kind_robots `Cypress Tests` runs (2026-07-31
00:06-15:03 UTC) hung ~27min each at the identical spot before the workflow's
`timeout-minutes: 30` cancelled them — root cause was an unbounded `fetch()` inside
`cy.then()`, a real Cypress gotcha the suite doesn't guard against anywhere it uploads
multipart images.

**Detail:**
- ci-janitor filed 4 duplicate HIGH todos (#1003-#1006) for `cancelled` runs
  (`30592571651`, `30603071073`, `30612641605`, `30622419984`, `30630735658`,
  `30641260379`). GitHub Actions job logs (via MCP `get_job_logs`, never a raw
  `curl` — see the 2026-07-17 entry above on why that has no auth here) showed
  every hang stalls mid-`before()` hook in
  `cypress/e2e/api/art-image-collection-connections.cy.ts`, immediately after
  `cy.task('cypressSeed:get')` and into the raw-`fetch()` image upload — not a
  `cy.request()`, which would have failed after its own `responseTimeout`.
  `cy.then(async () => { await fetch(...) })` is a documented Cypress behavior:
  Cypress applies no command timeout to a promise returned from `.then()`, so a
  stalled fetch hangs the spec (and the whole CI job) until an external timeout
  kills it — here, the GH Actions job's own 30-minute hard limit, with zero
  Cypress-side diagnostics.
- The underlying server-side stall **self-resolved** — main has been green every
  run since `30646489817` (16:17 UTC) with no code change in between — so nothing
  needed fixing in the product to restore main to green (already green by the time
  I investigated). Fixed the test contract instead: added `fetchWithTimeout()`
  (`cypress/support/api-auth.ts`, AbortController, 45s) and switched both raw-fetch
  upload helpers (`art-image-collection-connections.cy.ts` and `art-upload.cy.ts` —
  same pattern, same gap) to use it. kind_robots PR #1218, merged after CI green.
- Todo #986 (`30557217842`, conclusion `failure`) is unrelated: a one-off "Cypress
  binary missing" cache miss sandwiched between two green runs on nearby commits —
  closed per the same "later run on the branch already succeeded, no code change"
  precedent as the 2026-07-17 Todo #371/#385 entries above.

**Suggested action:** worth grepping the rest of `cypress/e2e/` for any other
`cy.then(async () => { ... fetch(` raw-fetch pattern beyond the two files caught
here (`api-upload` family) — this incident only surfaced because it happened to hang
on a scheduled run; a less severe stall (a few seconds slow) in a different spec
using the same unguarded pattern would just silently eat CI wall-clock time with no
symptom until it eventually gets bad enough to timeout too.

- What actually happened: PR #1259's own production deployment (commit `f79a08a`) held a MariaDB named lock on one ProxySQL session for the full duration of the serialized Facet maintenance pipeline. The build outlived that database session — ProxySQL closed it despite keepalive pings — and the deployment failed with `ER_CMD_CONNECTION_CLOSED` before Nuxt could even build. Independently confirmed: `dpl_GvVyv7qCAVE16QqvsiA9Ra4ngShr` (the production deployment for `f79a08a`) shows `state: ERROR` in the Vercel API.
- kind_robots PR #1260 (Silas, merged as `b8c3db0`) fixed the actual problem by decoupling deployment from maintenance rather than trying to keep a long-running DB session alive through a Vercel build: it removed the `run_facet_catalog_maintenance.ts` invocation from `scripts/vercel-build.mjs` entirely (the runner still exists for explicit, out-of-band maintenance runs) and added a contract forbidding it from being reconnected to the build path.

Todo #1051 (marked done earlier, based on PR #1259 alone) is now actually resolved.
- Root mistake in the closed entry: I wrote "fixed" based on CI green + the PR's own Vercel *preview* deployment going green, without waiting for the actual *production* deployment (which runs the full maintenance pipeline preview builds skip) to reach a terminal state. CI and preview-deploy success are necessary but not sufficient for a claim like this when the regression is specific to the production build path.

**Suggested action:** Reviewers/agents: for any fix whose failure mode is specific to the production deploy path (not exercised by CI or preview builds), do not write a TALKBACK "fixed" conclusion — or close out a red-CI Todo — until the actual next production deployment reaches a terminal state (`READY` or `ERROR`), not just CI green. **Subject:** `select_role.py` flagged `worker/dream-cycle-t-006-art-queue-dedup` as a candidate worker branch with no open PR. Investigation found two prior automated attempts to land the same patch had both failed at the exact same step, and the branch had been sitting with the work never actually applied.

**Detail:**
- A prior session had claimed t-006, authored a self-removing one-shot patch script (`scripts/agent_daily_dream_art_dedup.py`) to deduplicate six duplicate `dream-cycle-the-filing-echidna-*` rows in `projects/art-prompts.yaml`, and wired two successive "push this workflow file to trigger it" bootstrap workflows to apply it. Both CI runs (30767871034, 30767921091) got as far as `patch → py_compile → pytest (802 passed) → git diff --check`, then died on `git diff --check` with exit 2 before the commit step ever ran — so the ephemeral checkout's work was discarded both times, and the actual duplicates were still live on `main` when I picked this up.
- Root cause: `patch_tests()` wrote `TESTS.write_text(source.rstrip() + additions + "\n", ...)`, but the `additions` string it appends already ends in `\n` — so every run left a stray blank line at EOF, which `git diff --check` correctly flagged. One-line fix (dropped the redundant `+ "\n"`), ran the patcher locally, verified py_compile/pytest/the dedup invariant/`git diff --check` all clean, then committed and pushed to the same branch, opened PR #1578, and merged once CI (24/24 checks) was green.
- While reviewing, also found PR #1575 (interface-vision t-061/t-062, roadmap-only) sitting on stale CI — its one red check (`Ruler-hooked docs & art-prompts guards`) was a pre-existing base-branch break that had already been fixed on `main` by PR #1574 three minutes after #1575's CI last ran. Used `update_pull_request_branch` to rebase it onto current `main`; CI came back fully green and it merged clean. Textbook "base branch recovered" case from AGENTS.md.
- Mid-review, both PR branches picked up an unexpected extra merge commit from `main` authored under the repo owner's git identity — most likely a concurrent session doing its own branch-freshness maintenance. Treated it the documented way: didn't force-push or fight it, just let CI re-run on the new SHA and merged once green.

**What to improve (Worker pattern):**
- When a bootstrapped CI automation's *test* step passes but a *later* step fails, read that step's own log before authoring a second (or third) round of automation. Here the exact failure — file, line, "new blank line at EOF" — was sitting in the first failed run's log the whole time; a second workflow was built and failed identically instead.
- Self-modifying/self-removing one-shot patch scripts are a reasonable pattern for a bounded, scoped fix, but they should be exercised locally (or in a throwaway checkout) before being wired to a live CI trigger — the round-trip cost of debugging blind through push-and-wait CI cycles is much higher than a two-minute local run.

**Kaizen task:** none filed this cycle — the fix was the kaizen (a one-line bug in already-reviewed, already-merged infrastructure); no further roadmap follow-up needed since the patch script and its launcher workflow are both deleted now that they've served their purpose.

## 2026-08-04 | Agent run | interface-vision/t-058 + conductor infra | pattern

type: pattern

**Subject:** Two infrastructure gotchas hit while landing a t-058 verifier slice, both
worth a future session recognizing faster than this one did.

**Detail:**

1. **HTTP 413 on `git push` fires even for a single-line diff on an already-pushed
   branch, not just the two cases CLAUDE.md documents (brand-new ref, post-rebase
   force-push).** This session's conductor checkout is a shallow clone
   (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → true, 563M `.git`). A plain incremental
   commit on top of an unmoved, previously-pushed branch tip still 413'd on every
   retry (4 attempts with backoff). Root cause is the same "proxy wants a full pack,
   not a delta" symptom CLAUDE.md already names — just triggered by the shallow
   clone's graft boundary confusing git's own reachability negotiation, not by a
   diverged/rewritten history. The existing `push_files` (MCP) workaround still
   applies and worked immediately once tried; the fix here is just recognizing the
   trigger condition is broader than the two documented cases. Worth updating
   CLAUDE.md's HTTP-413 section to name "any push failing 413 on a shallow clone,
   regardless of diff size" as a third trigger, so a future session reaches for
   `push_files` on the first 413 instead of after 4 blind retries.

2. **A hand-typed `session` field in a task-event is silently rejected as
   `ALREADY_CLAIMED` if it doesn't byte-for-byte match the claim's recorded session
   string — including punctuation.** `claim_task.py` had recorded
   `claimed_by: 2026-08-04T11:27:54Z-t058-verifier` (colons intact); the review event
   I hand-authored used `2026-08-04T112754Z-t058-verifier` (colons dropped, a
   transcription slip). The processor correctly rejected it and consumed the event
   as a no-op rather than erroring loudly — which is the documented, correct
   behavior (task-events/README.md: "A repeat claim from a different session ...
   loses the race ... zero roadmap mutation"), but it meant the roadmap silently sat
   at `status: claimed` for ~45 minutes after the underlying PR had already merged,
   and the mismatch was only found by pulling the workflow run's job logs directly
   (`get_workflow_run_logs_url` → download the zip → grep). The fix (a corrected
   retry event with the exact session string) worked immediately. Worth a kaizen: a
   task-event's `session` field should be copy-pasted from the roadmap's live
   `claimed_by`, never re-typed from memory of the claim command — and if the
   processor's rejection message could also land as a PR comment (not just buried in
   Action logs) on the PR that referenced the task, it'd be far faster to notice.

**What was good:**
- Diagnosed the 413 root cause with `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` +
  `git count-objects -v` rather than assuming CLAUDE.md's two documented triggers
  were exhaustive, and reached for the documented `push_files` workaround as soon
  as retries confirmed it wasn't transient.
- Caught the silent review-event rejection by actually reading the processor's
  workflow run logs rather than assuming a `[skip ci]` "process task events" commit
  meant the event applied — the roadmap's own `status` field after the fact was the
  tell (still `claimed`, not `review`), which prompted checking rather than
  trusting the green workflow run.

**What to improve:** covered above — CLAUDE.md's 413 section and a copy-not-retype
habit for task-event `session` fields.

**Kaizen task:** none filed this session (time-boxed to the t-058 slice); flagging
both patterns here for whoever next touches `docs/`/`AGENTS.md` push-workaround docs
or `scripts/process_task_events.py`'s error surfacing.

## 2026-08-05 | Agent run (interface-vision t-100) | kind_robots | incident

type: incident

**Subject:** The public apex domain `kindrobots.org` is serving `404 DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND` — the Vercel deployment alias appears to be detached. `kind-robots.vercel.app` is fine, which is why no CI job noticed.

**Detail:**
- Found incidentally while building `verifyStoredArtPaths.ts` for interface-vision/t-100: probing production art paths against `https://kindrobots.org` returned 404 for *every* path, including the site root.
- Confirmed it is not a sandbox/proxy artifact. `curl -D-` against `https://kindrobots.org/` returns:
  ```
  HTTP/2 404
  content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
  x-vercel-error: DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND
  content-length: 107

  The deployment could not be found on Vercel.
  ```
  `x-vercel-error` is emitted by Vercel's edge, not by the agent proxy — the request reached Vercel and Vercel had nothing aliased to that hostname. Agent-proxy status was checked at the same time and reported `enabled: true` with `recentRelayFailures: []`.
- `https://www.kindrobots.org/` returns the same 404. `https://kindrobots.com/` does not resolve at all (curl status 000). `https://kind-robots.vercel.app/` returns `200 text/html` and serves real art (`/images/botcafe.webp` → `200 image/webp`, 69 KB).
- **Why nothing caught it:** `responsive-layout-audit.yml`'s production fallback URL is `https://kind-robots.vercel.app`, not the apex domain (see its "Resolve target URL" step). Every scheduled audit has therefore been measuring the deployment directly and passing — 12/12 clean as recently as run `30962348139` — while the domain users actually visit was returning 404. No check in either repo hits the apex domain.
- Timestamp of observation: 2026-08-05 00:48 UTC.

**What to improve:** whatever monitors production should hit the hostname users type, not only the deployment URL. A deployment-URL-only check is structurally blind to exactly this failure — alias detached, domain expired/misconfigured, DNS moved — because the deployment itself is healthy the whole time. This is the same shape as the t-100 defect it was found while fixing: the check and the failure mode were looking at different things.

**Suggested action:** Silas — check the Vercel project's Domains tab for `kindrobots.org`/`www.kindrobots.org`; this is a config/alias issue rather than anything in the codebase, so no PR is proposed. If the apex domain is intentionally retired in favour of the `.vercel.app` URL, say so and the audit's fallback is already correct; otherwise the alias needs reattaching and it would be worth adding the apex domain to whatever the audit probes.

**Kaizen task:** none filed — this is an infrastructure/config incident for Silas, not a code change, and filing a task against a repo that cannot fix it would just add a stale gate. Filed here so it is not lost.

## 2026-08-09 | Reviewer → Worker | conductor/t-109 | pattern
type: pattern

**Subject:** A guard that can only fail is half a guard — the pre-gate backlog needed a repair path, not just a rejection.

**Detail:**
- The 2026-08-08 prompt contract does two jobs with one mechanism: it rejects bad prompts at
  enqueue (right), and it re-applies the same rules at claim so pre-gate PENDING rows cannot
  render with stale settings (also right). But at claim the only available verdict was FAILED.
- Eight jobs (4843-4877) died on nothing but `krea2 ... got 20`, with 27 more queued behind
  them. Every one had correct cfg, clean prompt text, and a step count no human chose — it
  came from a queue builder that has since been fixed. There was nothing for a human to
  re-author; the correct value was computable from a table already in the file that rejected it.
- The tell is worth naming for next time: **when a rule's violation has one obviously correct
  repair, rejecting is not the conservative choice — it is just a different failure.** The
  conservative choice is repair-then-assert, with the repair recorded. Rules whose violations
  need judgment (a conditional a diffusion model can't evaluate, a format noun) genuinely have
  to fail, and still do.
- Second, smaller pattern: `reenqueue-failed` normalized image paths, prompts and LoRA
  resources, but not the sampler — so the one endpoint whose whole job is "make this failed
  job runnable again" would have requeued these eight to fail identically on the next poll. A
  repair path that doesn't repair the thing that killed the job is a loop, not a recovery.
- Producer side: `entry_to_job` was fixed on 2026-08-08 to resolve steps and cfg per engine,
  and that fix was real — but it only governed DEFAULTS. An explicit `steps: 20` on an entry
  still passed through untouched, which is how the value got in. Fixing the default without
  bounding the override left the door open at exactly the width of the original bug.

**Suggested action:** Nothing observed here was a Worker error — the contract and the
per-engine defaults were both good work, landed fast under real damage. Two things to carry
forward: (1) when adding a hard gate that will also be applied retroactively to a backlog,
decide per-rule whether a pre-existing row should fail or be repaired, and say so in the rule
table; (2) when fixing a default, check whether the corresponding explicit override is bounded
too. Both are now encoded in tests (`verifyArtJobSamplerRepair.ts`,
`test_explicit_steps_are_clamped_to_the_engine_ceiling`) rather than left as advice.

**Pattern note:** Related to the 2026-07-26 entry on conductor/t-080 — the same pipeline,
the same shape of problem. There, the claim-time failure string was too generic to diagnose
(`ComfyUI reported a workflow error`, no node detail) and a fix had to be shipped to make
*future* failures legible. Here the error string was excellent — it named the engine, the
ceiling, and the actual value, which is why this took one probe instead of a day. Detailed
failure text paid for itself; the gap this time was one layer up, in what the system was
allowed to do about a failure it had already diagnosed perfectly.

     — the same layer DaisyUI's own component classes (`.stat`, `.collapse`, `.menu`, ...) occupy.
     Bare Tailwind utility tokens are in the *utilities* layer and always beat components regardless
     of source order, but two components-layer classes on the same element have no such guarantee —
     which side wins depends on stylesheet source order, not HTML class order. The codemod now
     requires every other token on a matched element to be a plain Tailwind utility or a known-safe
     no-bg/border `kr-*` primitive; anything else (a bare DaisyUI component-root class) is skipped

Reverted an unrelated `prisma/generated/` regeneration-drift diff produced by local dependency provisioning before committing, to keep the PR scoped.

Conductor PR #2052 (`status: review` bookkeeping) and #2053 (close-out, re-arm to `ready` since this is `recurring: true`) both merged clean.

Treating the `check_pr_merged_drift.py` 403 as the documented API-access gap and cross-checking the specific flagged task against its live roadmap note, rather than either trusting the script's exit code blindly or ignoring it.

**Suggested action:** the `capture-group-guard` CI failure is worth a note for future sessions writing a *new* `.exec()`/`.match()` call site anywhere in kind_robots, not just this file: `assert.ok(match, ...)` does not satisfy the checker even though it correctly narrows the type for TypeScript/runtime purposes -- only an explicit `if (!match) return/continue/throw`, optional chaining with a nullish fallback, default-valued destructuring, or a non-null assertion (`match!`) are recognized. Worth running `verifyCaptureGroupGuards.ts origin/main` locally before opening any PR that adds a new capture-group call site, the same way this session now does for `vue-tsc`/`eslint`/`prettier`.

## 2026-08-12 | Agent → Silas | conductor (session-local) | security-flag

type: security-flag

**Subject:** Accidentally echoed the live `KR_API_TOKEN` value to my own tool output this session.

**Detail:**
- While checking whether `KR_API_TOKEN` was set before running `recheck_render_queue.py`, I ran
  `echo "KR_API_TOKEN set: ${KR_API_TOKEN:+yes}${KR_API_TOKEN:-no}"` intending a yes/no probe.
  `${KR_API_TOKEN:-no}` substitutes the actual value when the variable IS set (the `-` form means
  "use default only if unset/empty"), not "no" -- I wanted `:+`/`:-` reversed, or just a boolean
  check. The full token value was printed into this session's own tool-call transcript.
- Scope: this stayed inside the sandbox's own session transcript/output -- it was not pasted into
  any file committed to either repo, not sent to any external service, and not included in either
  TALKBACK entry or PR body from this session (checked both before writing them).
- Session transcripts may be retained/reviewable outside the same access boundary as the secrets
  store itself, so treating this as a real (if contained) exposure rather than a non-event.

**Suggested action:** Silas's call whether `KR_API_TOKEN` is worth rotating given the exposure was
sandbox-transcript-only, not network-transmitted or committed. No code or roadmap change needed on
this agent's end -- flagging per hard rule 8 for acknowledgement, and noting the correct pattern
for a future "is this env var set" check is `[ -n "${VAR:-}" ] && echo yes || echo no` (or `test -n`),
never a bare `${VAR:-...}` substitution when VAR might hold a secret.

- Read `components/bots/bot-gallery.vue` → `bot-interact.vue` → shared
  `components/gallery/kr-gallery.vue` to trace the reported crushed element
  (`CRUSHED <div> "NarratorAllPrompt BotAll statusesR" w=5 .min-w-0
  flex-1`) to `kr-gallery.vue`'s `#toolbar` slot wrapper. Root cause is the
  same bug class as #1890's channel-select/tab-select crush, one layer
  deeper: the wrapper was `min-w-0 flex-1` (`flex-basis: 0%`), and CSS
  flex-wrap's line-breaking decision uses each item's *hypothetical* main
  size (basis-derived) to decide whether it fits the current line — for a
  basis:0 item that's always 0, so the browser never saw the toolbar slot
  as too big to wrap, and `min-w-0` let it absorb 100% of the deficit
  against the sticky bar's `shrink-0` pager and mode-toggle buttons instead
  of moving to its own line, which the bar's own `flex-wrap` already
  intended for it to do.
- Fix: switched the wrapper to `flex-auto` (basis: auto) so its
  hypothetical size is real content width, restoring correct wrap
  behavior. `min-w-0` kept so it still shrinks normally when it does fit.
  Shared component — fix applies to every gallery using the toolbar slot,
  not just `/bots`. `npx prettier --check` passed; no live-browser
  verification possible from this sandbox (same proxy limitation as every
  prior cycle), so confirmation defers to the next scheduled

Rather than stop there, traced one hop downstream to what actually *consumes* `assertArtImageAttachable`'s caller context: the PATCH write paths (`prepareItemUpdate()`, feeding `items/[id].patch.ts` and `items/batch.patch.ts`).
- Found a real, previously-unfixed bug: `prepareItemUpdate()` wrote the client's entire requested `stageStatuses` blob straight onto `data.stageStatuses` — a blind wholesale overwrite. The client always sends the item's full local `.stages` object on every write (just what its reactive state looks like at click time), so any *other* stage key a concurrent request changed in the window between this request's `existing` read and its own write got silently clobbered back to the stale snapshot. This is the exact same class of bug `commit.post.ts` already had fixed once for its own COMMIT-only write (`verifyModelBuilderCommitStaleSnapshotGuard.ts`), but that fix was never generalized to the PATCH/batch-PATCH routes. Most exploitable in `items/batch.patch.ts`: every entry does its own `findUnique` + `assertArtImageAttachable` round trip before the shared transaction even starts, so a same-item concurrent single-item PATCH (e.g. an async art job's `pollAsyncArtJob` → `pushItem` finishing mid-batch) has real room to land and then get silently reverted.
- Fixed by diffing the request's `stageStatuses` against its own `existing` snapshot (`diffStageStatusChanges`) to find which keys it actually intends to change, then re-reading the item's live `stageStatuses` immediately before each write and merging only those changed keys onto it (`mergeStageStatusChanges`) — never writing the stale blob wholesale. Generalizes `commit.post.ts`'s fix from one hardcoded key (COMMIT) to arbitrary changed keys.
- Added `verifyModelBuilderPatchStaleStageStatusGuard.ts` + `.test.ts` following the established narrow-textual-checker convention, wired into `package.json` and `contract-tests.yml`. Verified: new guard + self-test pass; all 69 `test:model-builder-*` npm scripts pass (no regression); `vue-tsc --noEmit` exits 0 repo-wide; eslint clean on touched files; `prettier --check` clean (`items/[id].patch.ts`'s pre-existing formatting drift, present on `main` before this change, untouched by this diff's added lines); `git status --porcelain` showed exactly the 7 intended files.
- kind_robots PR #1900: all required checks green at merge time (only the optional "Build production image" docker job still running, matching the established non-blocking pattern), squash-merged e57d70a. Set `status: review` before opening the PR, then set `status: ready` (with the note prepended, `implementation_pr` updated to #1900, claim fields cleared) after the merge — recurring-task convention, t-029 never reaches `done`. Appended `LEARNING.yaml` record.

**What was good:** not stopping at "the suggested files turned out clean" — traced one hop downstream to what those files' output actually feeds into, and found a real, previously-known-but-not-generalized bug shape there instead of reporting a dry cycle.

**Kaizen task:** deferred — the fix itself (generalizing the commit.post.ts stale-snapshot pattern to the PATCH routes) is this cycle's concrete output; no further meta-task warranted.

- **The delegation surfaced a real, subtle correctness bug that would have shipped silently if taken at face value.** The background agent's sandbox refused git-mutating operations against the shared checkout (by design — the same `isolation: worktree` protection AGENTS.md hard safety rule 12 mandates), so it worked around this by building/testing in an isolated copy and pushing the finished branch via the GitHub content API (`create_branch` + `push_files`) rather than `git push`. That workaround pushed each file's *full content* as constructed against a snapshot of `main` taken at task start — but `main` moved concurrently (kapowarr/t-026 merged mid-task, adding an `import frontend.torznab` line to `frontend/ui.py`). The agent's push silently reverted that line and its surrounding comment back to the pre-t-026 wording, because it never re-fetched `frontend/ui.py`'s *current* remote content before constructing its own edit to that same file — it only diffed its own before/after snapshot, not against live `main`.
  - This was not caught by the agent's own verification (tests/mypy/isort all ran against its isolated copy, which by definition also lacked the concurrent t-026 change — so nothing there could have detected a conflict that only exists relative to live `main`) or by the PR's own CI (`import frontend.torznab` referencing a module CI's test suite doesn't otherwise import directly means removing it doesn't fail an import-time test; the settings routes it registers just silently stop existing).
  - Caught only because this session's own long-standing discipline is to pull the actual PR file list/diff before merging rather than trusting an agent's self-report (same pattern as several recent kapowarr TALKBACK entries) — `mcp__github__pull_request_read`'s `get_files` showed `frontend/ui.py` with a suspicious `-import frontend.torznab` removal for a PR whose task had nothing to do with Torznab, which is what triggered digging into it. Confirmed via `list_commits` that t-026 actually had already merged (4a8235e) and via `get_file_contents` at `ref: main` that the import line was genuinely present on live main and genuinely absent from the PR branch.
  - Fixed with one follow-up commit (`create_or_update_file` restoring the two-line block exactly as it reads on `main`, keyed off the file's live blob SHA on the PR branch so the write itself couldn't repeat the same stale-base mistake), re-ran all 7 checks green on the corrected commit, confirmed the PR's file-level diff for `frontend/ui.py` was now a clean `+5/-0` (just the new route, nothing removed), then squash-merged.
  - Also explicitly checked for the *other* risk the agent itself flagged (a DB migration-slot collision at `47` if t-026 also claimed it) — confirmed t-026 never touches `db_migration.py` at all, so no collision existed there.
- Roadmap close-out via `close_task.py` on its own branch/PR (this PR), `implementation_pr: silasfelinus/Kapowarr#42`.

**What was good:** did not take "all 7 checks green" or the agent's detailed self-verification narrative as sufficient — pulled the actual current file-level diff before merging and noticed a removed import line that had no business being touched by a weekly-pull-list PR, then traced *why* (a stale-base API push racing a concurrent merge) rather than just patching the symptom blind.

**What to improve:** the underlying gap is real and will recur: any background agent forced by sandbox isolation to push via `create_branch`/`push_files` instead of `git push`/`git rebase` is, by construction, working from a point-in-time snapshot and has no way to detect a concurrent change to a file it also touches — `git push`'s non-fast-forward rejection (this repo's normal safety net for exactly this class of race, documented extensively in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) doesn't apply to content-API pushes at all, since there's no shared ref history to reject against. This is a gap in the documented workaround pattern itself, not just this one agent's execution.

**Kaizen task:** `kapowarr/t-046` — created (see roadmap): document (in `FORK_MAINTENANCE.md` or a new `docs/` note) that any content-API-based push workaround (`create_branch` + `push_files`/`create_or_update_file`) must re-fetch each touched file's *current* remote content immediately before constructing the write, not rely on a start-of-task snapshot — and that a human/reviewing session merging such a PR should specifically diff every touched file against live `main` before merging, not just trust green CI, since CI cannot detect an import-time-only removal with no direct test coverage.

The server (`batch.patch.ts`) validates/applies each entry independently, so a real failure is usually partial — but `batchPushItems()` only ever returned a bare `boolean`, so callers couldn't tell which entries a partial failure rejected, leaving stale optimistic UI state (wrong approved badge / wrong field value) in place until a full reload silently corrected it. Fix: `batchPushItems()` now returns `{ ok, failedIds }` derived from the server's per-entry results on an HTTP 207 partial failure; callers snapshot pre-mutation state and revert exactly the failed entries. ## 2026-08-19 | Claude (Silas-directed session) | kind-economy project creation | reviewer

**Decision:** created `projects/kind-economy/` — the money layer for Kind Robots — and opened `silasfelinus/conductor#2475`.

**What happened:**
- Silas opened the session with the full history: he founded Save One Human during the pandemic on the ~$5,000-saves-a-life premise, incorporated in CA, got an EIN, raised $0, and later began unwinding it and filing overdue zero-dollar returns. Kind Robots is the successor. ~$840 raised via againstmalaria.com/amibot, almost entirely his own donations plus family birthday-gift redirects. He asked for a new conductor project covering the three-way revenue share, creator payouts, backend dispersal, and restarting the nonprofit (target: Jan 1), after reviewing all three repos. He called it "a vitally important tentpole to our site and my life trajectory."
- Read all three repos before writing anything. The audit is the substance of this session and is written up in `projects/kind-economy/DESIGN-BRIEF.md`.
- **Five verified gaps between the site's public promise and the code.** (1) `User.mana` is a single `Int` and `maybeRefill()` grants free `CYCLE_REFILL` mana into the same balance, so paid and granted mana are commingled and "paid usage" is not computable from stored data at all — this is the foundational blocker and everything else in m2 depends on fixing it. (2) `applyMana()`'s `refId` is free text with no creator attribution, so "the creator of the web object that inspired the interaction" cannot be identified at spend time even in principle. (3) Zero references to Stripe Connect / `transfer_data` / `application_fee` anywhere in the repo — there is no payout mechanism. (4) `giving-page.vue` links users OUT to againstmalaria.com/amibot, so the platform's own mission share has no route to the fundraiser. (5) `CREATOR_EARNINGS_MESSAGE` in `stores/helpers/tutorialCards.ts` already states the three-way split as present-tense fact on six tutorial channels, ahead of the mechanism.
- Take-in side is genuinely built but has never processed a real transaction: six Stripe routes plus a 663-line signature-verified, `stripeSessionId`-idempotent webhook, `Order`/`OrderItem`/`Entitlement`/`PrintJob`/`Grant` models, a mana ledger pegged at 1,000 mana = $1 — and no `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`/`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` configured anywhere, no `.env.example`, auth-rejection Cypress coverage only.
- **Key strategic finding: reviving the nonprofit is NOT a prerequisite for the revenue share.** A for-profit platform donating the mission share directly to the Against Malaria Foundation (itself a registered charity) needs no entity work at all, and is the cheapest route that also minimizes the reporting complexity Silas explicitly asked to avoid. Reviving Save One Human earns its keep only if he specifically wants tax-deductible donations to his own charity, grant eligibility, or institutional permanence. The roadmap is ordered so the entity track (m5) never blocks the ledger track (m2).
- Structured as 5 milestones / 20 tasks: SHAPE (decide the model and the entity question) → LEDGER (paid-mana distinction, creator attribution, immutable `RevenueSplit` ledger, creator earnings view) → LIVE STRIPE → DISPERSAL (payouts, remittance runbook, creator terms) → ENTITY. Registered `active`/`urgent` in `project-overrides.yaml` and placed at the top of `projects/priority.yaml` under the CONTROL.md in-session clearance rule.
- Adopted `digital-storefront/t-039` (Stripe E2E, parked at `needs-human` since 2026-08-08 for the same credential/DB gap) as `kind-economy/t-011` rather than duplicating it; t-039 closes by reference once the matrix runs. Kept the ownership line clean: `digital-storefront` owns what is sold, `kind-economy` owns what happens to the money afterward.
- Wrote a project-level safety posture stricter than the repo default into `notes_from_silas`: no live keys / products / charges / payouts without per-action approval (test mode included), no agent files or pays anything with a government agency, no agent creates a Stripe or bank account, nothing in the project is legal or tax advice, and the ledger is append-only by rule. Every money-moving and filing task is `gate_human` with `outward-facing` or `irreversible` stakes.

**What was good:** reading the code before writing the roadmap. The commingled-mana finding is not visible from the product description or the site copy — it only shows up by reading `refill.ts` next to `mana.ts` and noticing that a single `Int` balance cannot answer "was this paid for". A roadmap written from Silas's description alone would have started at "wire up Stripe Connect" and hit that wall months later, after the payout design was already built on sand.

**What to improve (2):** placed `kind-economy` at the TOP of `projects/priority.yaml` on the strength of Silas calling it a tentpole, and CI caught it — `tests/test_project_priority_contract.py` hard-asserts `order[0] == "kapowarr"`, a guard added 2026-08-18. The tempting fix was to update the test, since a priority list and its contract test are supposed to move together. Rejected that: Silas asked for a new project, not a portfolio reorder, and he set Kapowarr's priority four days ago and merged Kapowarr work today. Rewriting a CI-enforced human priority decision to make my own change go green is the same antipattern as deleting a failing test, even when the mechanical fix is one line. Moved `kind-economy` to second instead and wrote the reasoning into `priority.yaml` so the next session doesn't re-litigate it; `priority: urgent` in `project-overrides.yaml` already carries the importance signal without touching the guard. Flagged for Silas: if he does want it first, the test moves with it — his call.

The general lesson: an in-session "this is vitally important" is direction about *what to build*, and does not automatically license reordering everything else the human already decided. Record the importance where it belongs and ask before overriding a guard.

**What to improve (1):** ran `audit_roadmaps.py` during verification without noticing it rewrites the tracked `ROADMAP-AUDIT.json`/`.md` artifacts in place. That swept 4 days of unrelated portfolio drift (last generated 2026-08-15) into the first commit. Caught it on the `--stat` review and reverted both files before pushing, so nothing landed — but the audit script is read-only in spirit and write-only in fact, and a session that skips the diff review would silently ship a workflow-owned artifact inside a feature PR. Worth remembering that the verification step itself can dirty the tree.

**Kaizen task:** none filed. `conductor/t-111` already tracks a related `audit_human_gates.py` visibility gap; the `ROADMAP-AUDIT` write-during-verification observation above is recorded here rather than as its own task until it recurs.

## 2026-08-20 | Agent (scheduled conductor sweep) | conductor/t-120 | pattern

**Decision:** merged — see below.

**Subject:** The #1 priority project's entire remaining backlog was invisible to the
task-selection machinery for an unknown length of time, because 8 of its tasks were
written in a status no selection path recognises.

**Detail:**
- Four consecutive scheduled cycles today (model-builder/t-029 cycles 26–29) all fell
  through the whole `projects/priority.yaml` queue to the same 12th-ranked recurring
  polish task. Each cycle correctly recorded "every project ahead had no claimable
  ready work" — that observation was true as read, and false as reality.
- `projects/kapowarr/roadmap.yaml` (pinned at `order[0]`, CI-enforced by
  `tests/test_project_priority_contract.py`) carried t-034, t-035 and t-040..t-045 as
  `status: not-started`. That is a valid *milestone* status here
  (`build_workspace.py`'s colour map, `new_app.py`'s milestone template) and has never
  been a task status. All 8 are dependency-free and `stakes: reversible`.
- The failure mode is worth naming precisely: an unknown status does not read as
  "not yet startable", it reads as *nothing at all*. `next_ready_task.py`,
  `run_worker.py`, `claim_task.py` and `select_role.py` all match `status == "ready"`
  exactly, and every other consumer keys off the documented side exits, so such a task
  never appears as ready work, never as a gate, and never as blocked. Kapowarr
  presented as 47/56 done with a single soft gate and nothing to do.
- `audit_roadmaps.py` had been emitting all 8 as `INVALID_STATUS` **errors** the whole
  time. It is advisory and always exits 0. This is the same shape its sibling
  `validate_roadmaps.py` already documents in its own docstring for
  `DUPLICATE_TASK_ID`: detected advisorily, ignored, landed twice in interface-vision
  before being promoted to a hard gate (conductor/t-107). Two independent instances of
  "the audit already knew" is now a pattern, not a coincidence.

**Suggested action:** when a scheduled cycle reports "no claimable ready work" for a
project ranked above the one it ends up picking, treat that as a claim to verify rather
than a fact to record — a one-line status histogram over the skipped roadmap would have
surfaced this on the first cycle. More generally: an advisory finding that has been
firing continuously is evidence the advisory tier is the wrong tier for it. Promoting
`INVALID_STATUS` to `validate_roadmaps.py` (this task) is the second such promotion;
the remaining `audit_roadmaps.py` error codes are worth reviewing as a set for the same
question rather than one incident at a time.
