## 2026-08-20 | Agent (scheduled conductor sweep) | kapowarr/t-035 | pattern

**Decision:** cleared a stranded branch that appeared on `origin` *after* this session had
already closed the task it belonged to. No data lost; recording it because it is a fresh,
same-day instance of a failure mode AGENTS.md documents at length.

**Detail:**
- Sequence, all on 2026-08-20: this session pushed t-035's `review` transition via
  `close_task.py` at ~15:29 onto `close/kapowarr-t-035-sched-20260820T1520Z-kapowarr-t035`;
  Kapowarr#83 merged; conductor#2573 landed the `done` transition and merged at ~15:35,
  auto-deleting its branch. Then at **15:36:42** a branch named
  `reviewer/close-kapowarr-t035` appeared, carrying a single commit
  `close: kapowarr/t-035 -> status=review` — quoting **this session's own session id** —
  with no PR.
- `close_task.py` cannot have produced that name: its `default_branch_name()` is
  `close/<project>-<task-id>-<session-slug>`, and nothing in `scripts/` or
  `.github/workflows/` emits a `reviewer/close-*` ref. So it came from somewhere outside
  this session's own tooling, reusing the session id it would have read from the roadmap's
  `claimed_by` field.
- The branch's diff would have reverted `t-035` from `done` back to `review`, discarding
  the `implementation_pr` link to Kapowarr#83. It never merged — there was no PR to merge
  it — so nothing was lost. Verified superseded against `main` (t-035 `done`,
  `implementation_pr: silasfelinus/Kapowarr#83`) before clearing it via `branch-janitor`
  with `force_delete_branches`; `git push --delete` 403s from this session as documented.
- Two things this sharpens about the existing rotation-collision guidance:
  1. **A losing session's artifact can outlive the winning session's close-out.** The
     documented cases all describe collisions detected at push time, where git's
     non-fast-forward rejection is the backstop. That backstop never engaged here, because
     the loser wrote to a *different ref* rather than racing for the same one. Nothing
     rejected anything; the stale state just sat there.
  2. **Reusing a session id across sessions makes the trail lie.** The commit reads as
     though this session pushed it, which is exactly why it took a look at
     `default_branch_name()` to establish that it hadn't. AGENTS.md already asks for
     collision-resistant session ids for the `claimed_by`/TALKBACK trail's sake; this is
     the same argument reaching one step further — an id copied *out of* the roadmap by a
     second actor forges attribution rather than merely blurring it.

**Suggested action:** nothing urgent — no loss occurred and the branch is gone. Two things
worth considering when someone next touches this area: whether the close-out path should
refuse to write a transition that moves a task *backwards* (`done` → `review`), which would
have made this a loud failure at push time instead of a silent stranded ref; and, per the
previous entry, that a branch pushed **without** a PR is invisible to every hygiene check
in both repos — this is the second instance found in one session, after the two stranded
Kapowarr branches noted above.

## 2026-08-20 | Agent (scheduled conductor sweep) | kapowarr/t-035 | incident

**Decision:** duplicate work discarded — both PRs closed unmerged, no `main` touched.

**Subject:** A scheduled session implemented, tested and opened a PR for a task another
session had already claimed and was actively finishing, because it read `status: claimed`
out of a stale local checkout and never ran `claim_task.py`.

**What happened:**
- Opening sweep found `kapowarr/t-035` at `status: claimed`, `claimed_by:
  sched-20260820T1520Z-kapowarr-t035`, with the claim commit (`09c1a4f`) already present
  in this session's local branch history. That local presence is what made the claim look
  like this session's own. It was not — it belonged to a concurrent session on
  `claude/beautiful-hawking-hysoh6`.
- Step 6 of AGENTS.md ("Claim it before doing real work") was skipped entirely, on the
  reasoning that a task already at `claimed` did not need claiming. That reasoning is
  exactly backwards: `claim_task.py` is what *establishes whose* claim it is, and it
  would have exited `ALREADY_CLAIMED` in one command against `origin/main`.
- ~40 minutes of implementation followed: a full NZBGet client, 32 tests, green local
  suite, silasfelinus/Kapowarr#84 opened.
- The collision only surfaced when a routine `actions_list` call to check CI returned
  workflow runs for silasfelinus/Kapowarr#83 — the other session's identical feature,
  same two file paths, squash-merged to `main` as `41019cb` at 15:29 UTC, roughly while
  this session was writing its own version.
- Worse than the wasted work: this session had already run `close_task.py ... review`
  passing `--session sched-20260820T1520Z-kapowarr-t035` — the *other* session's id,
  copied out of the roadmap because it was assumed to be this session's own. The
  ownership check had nothing to reject. Conductor PR #2575 would have regressed t-035
  from `done` back to `review` had it merged. It landed only on its own branch, so `main`
  was never touched, and both PRs are now closed with explanatory comments.

**What was good:** the merged implementation was read carefully before this one was
discarded, rather than either merging on top of it or assuming duplicate meant
equivalent. It is better on two points, and both are real bugs this session's version
had: #83 treats NZBGet history as terminal and imports only `SUCCESS/*` plus
`WARNING/SCRIPT`, where this version imported every `WARNING/*` — which would hand
`WARNING/PASSWORD` and `WARNING/DAMAGED` jobs to the importer and import an encrypted or
broken archive as if it were the comic; and its `delete_download` logs-and-returns on a
malformed id instead of raising into the download-queue polling loop. Nothing was worth
salvaging, and saying so is the right outcome rather than finding a way to land
something.

**What to improve — two concrete gaps, both mechanical:**

1. **`claim_task.py` has no "am I the claimant?" mode, so nothing catches this.** Every
   guard in the system is built around the `ready -> claimed` transition. Once a task is
   at `claimed`, a session that believes the claim is its own has no command to check
   that belief, and `close_task.py` accepts whatever `--session` it is handed. A session
   resuming after compaction is in exactly this position by design (AGENTS.md's
   "Same-session post-compaction collisions" already describes the state, and prescribes
   `git fetch` + diff — but only for the *wrap-up* step, not before implementation).
   Suggested: `claim_task.py --verify <project> <task-id> --session <id>`, exiting
   non-zero when `claimed_by` does not match, and `close_task.py` refusing a transition
   whose `--session` does not match live `claimed_by` unless `--force`. The second half
   is the one that would have converted this from a silent near-miss into a hard stop.

2. **CI status was checked ~50 minutes into the run; the collision was visible from the
   first minute.** `list_pull_requests(state=open)` on both repos returned `[]` during
   the opening sweep, which read as "nothing in flight" — but the other session's PR #83
   had not been opened yet, and by the time it existed *and* merged it was no longer
   open, so an open-PR check could never have seen it in either window. What would have
   seen it: `list_commits` / `actions_list` on the target repo's `main`, or simply
   `git fetch origin main` in the implementation repo before starting to write code.
   Suggested: fetch the *implementation* repo's `main` at claim time, not just the
   conductor roadmap. A task whose feature already exists on the target repo's `main` is
   the cheapest possible collision signal and nothing currently looks for it.

**Suggested action:** AGENTS.md's "Rotation collisions" section documents three variants
(concurrent pickup, post-compaction resume, concurrent PR-conflict resolution). This is a
fourth and it is the one with no mechanical guard at all: *inherited-claim mistaken for
own claim*. The other three are caught by `claim_task.py`'s atomic check or by a
non-fast-forward push rejection. This one produced a clean local test suite, a clean
push, a clean PR and green-looking CI, and was caught only by an incidental API call. The
`--verify` flag above is a small change to a script that already exists and would close
it.

**Kaizen task:** worth filing against `conductor` — "`close_task.py` should refuse a
transition whose `--session` does not match live `claimed_by`", carrying the
`claim_task.py --verify` half as the same change. Not filed from this session, which has
already demonstrated it was working from bad assumptions about claim ownership; it should
be filed by a session that can check the claim-ownership invariants across all the
scripts at once rather than patching in the shape of this one incident.

## 2026-08-23 | Agent (scheduled conductor sweep) → self | davinci/t-025 | pattern

**Subject:** two reusable process notes from a shared-extraction refactor task.

**Detail:**
- A task scoped as "extract the shared pattern between these two call sites" should
  grep the whole repo for the symbol/pattern being extracted before scoping the
  composable, not just the two files the task note already names. davinci/t-025
  missed a third, byte-for-byte identical call site (`stores/taskmasterStore.ts`)
  this way — caught only because a repo-owned contract test
  (`verifyNarrativeArtPersistence.mjs`) enforced the two known stores stay in
  lockstep and failed CI on the first push. A project without that kind of
  cross-file contract test would have silently shipped a partial extraction.
- Running `prettier --write` on a whole pre-existing file to clean up formatting
  around one targeted edit can reformat large unrelated regions if that file was
  already prettier-noncompliant on `main` before the change (confirmed here via
  `git checkout`/`git stash` on two separate files). When a file isn't already known
  to be prettier-clean, apply the intended edit via a scoped string replacement
  instead of a full-file `--write`, then verify with `--check` rather than
  `--write`, to keep the diff to exactly what the task touches.

**Suggested action:** worth a line in AGENTS.md's general guidance (not just this
project's TALKBACK) if a second instance of either pattern turns up — filed as
LEARNING.yaml lessons (davinci/t-025 record) in the meantime rather than editing
AGENTS.md from a single occurrence.

## 2026-08-24 | Reviewer (session incident) | conductor/scripts | security

**Decision:** SECURITY INCIDENT — self-inflicted `KR_API_TOKEN` leak into this
session's own tool-output transcript. Recommend rotating `KR_API_TOKEN` out of
caution. Flagging as hard needs-human (credential rotation is a secrets action
neither agent may perform).

**What happened:** While starting a session-start sweep, this session hand-rolled
a presence check instead of using `scripts/kr_token_set.sh`:

```
echo "KR_API_TOKEN is: ${KR_API_TOKEN:+SET}${KR_API_TOKEN:-UNSET}"
```

This is the *exact* anti-pattern `kr_token_set.sh`'s own header comment
documents and warns against (conductor/t-116, two prior instances on
2026-08-12 and 2026-08-13): `${VAR:-fallback}` only substitutes the fallback
when the variable is unset/empty — once `KR_API_TOKEN` is set, that second
expansion evaluates to the *live token value*, not the literal string
`"UNSET"`. The full JWT was printed into this session's Bash tool output and
is now present in this session's transcript/context.

This session had **already read** `kr_token_set.sh`'s warning comment
immediately beforehand (it was inspecting the script to understand why an
earlier `source scripts/kr_token_set.sh` call in a fresh shell hadn't
propagated `KR_API_TOKEN` to a subsequent tool call — this sandbox does not
persist shell env vars between Bash tool invocations, so the sourcing was a
no-op) and reproduced the documented mistake anyway while writing an ad hoc
diagnostic one-liner. This is the third documented occurrence of this same
leak pattern.

**Scope of exposure:** sandbox-only, not committed to git, not transmitted to
any external service — consistent with the two prior instances. The token
value is present in this session's own conversation transcript/logs, which is
"a real leak into a place it doesn't need to be" per `kr_token_set.sh`'s own
framing of the prior incidents, even without external transmission.

**Recommended action for Silas:**
1. Rotate `KR_API_TOKEN` (issue a fresh JWT for the automation account and
   update wherever it's configured for scheduled sessions) — this session
   cannot do this itself (secrets are a hard "neither agent" boundary).
2. Consider whether a *third* recurrence of a documented, actively-warned-
   against pattern means the mitigation needs to be stronger than a comment
   — e.g., a session-start reminder, or restructuring `KR_API_TOKEN` handling
   so no agent session ever needs to hand-probe presence at all (always
   pipe through `kr_token_set.sh`, or have calling scripts self-report
   presence via their own stderr the way `fetch_todos.py` already does,
   removing the need for a human-typed probe entirely).

**Kaizen task:** filed as `conductor/t-128` (see roadmap) — harden or remove
the need for hand-typed `KR_API_TOKEN` presence checks, given this is the
third real-world recurrence of the same documented leak.

  and only then does the `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` migration land, in its own PR. Landing
  the migration alongside the schema edit would reproduce the t-071 outage in reverse.
- Implemented step 1 exactly as specified (silasfelinus/kind_robots#2110): `prisma validate`,
  `prisma generate`, `vue-tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, and
  `utils/scripts/verifyCharacterMutationInputParity.ts` all clean; confirmed no live code
  reads `Character.size` anywhere in the app (only `characterBrowseSelect`/
  `characterMutationSelect`/`dreamCharacterSelect`, none of which selected it).
- CI's "Schema Migration Parity" check (`utils/scripts/verifySchemaMigrationParity.ts` /
  `schemaMigrationParity.ts`) failed it -- correctly, per its own design: it unconditionally
  requires a matching `prisma/migrations/*` file for any structural `prisma/schema.prisma`
  diff, with no annotation/label/config escape hatch for "this one's deferred on purpose."
  First re-run attempt hit an unrelated ~5min `git fetch` hang that self-cancelled (transient,
  re-ran clean on the underlying logic) before surfacing this real failure on the second run.
- This is a genuine conflict between two safety mechanisms that both trace back to real
  production incidents (t-071 in each direction) -- not a mistake on either side. Filed as
  `needs-human` (soft) with the PR left open, unmerged, rather than overriding a failing
  required check or dropping the task's own explicit sequencing to satisfy CI. Three options
  laid out for Silas in the roadmap note: (a) add a narrow, explicit deferred-migration escape
  hatch to the parity check, (b) Silas merges #2110 directly as a conscious override, (c) land
  the migration now anyway and manage the Force-Update timing by hand (not recommended -- the
  exact trap the task itself warns about).

**Suggested action:** If Silas picks option (a), the escape hatch should be narrow and
explicit by construction (e.g. a `Schema-Migration-Deferred: <reason>` trailer the check
greps for) so it can't quietly launder an ordinary forgotten migration -- not a blanket
skip flag. Worth checking whether any other schema task already worked around this gap by
just including the migration despite similar reverse-order risk; none found in this
session's TALKBACK sweep, but this may be the first DROP-shaped task to hit the check.

## 2026-08-25 | Reviewer → Worker | system | pattern
type: pattern

**Subject:** Three separate render-failure "incidents" tracked since 2026-08-21 are one
unreadable network drive on the render box, and nothing in the repo could resubmit the
backlog they produced.

**Detail:**
- Silas asked for the art queue's errors to be corrected and the jobs resubmitted. The
  queue held 420 FAILED ArtJobs: 100% COMFY, 100% at `attempts=3`, in two bursts —
  157 on 2026-08-21 (all `facet-catalog`) and 263 on 2026-08-25 (`cthulhuquarium` +
  `dream-cycle`).
- `ai-art-academy/t-068` has tracked the 08-21 burst since 08-15 as a facet-catalog
  problem in the `CLIPTextEncode` node. That framing was wrong, and the 08-25 burst
  proves it: the same box in the same hours produced **both** `hostbuf_file_reader_read
  failed` (224 jobs, node 3) **and** `[WinError 1117] ... I/O device error:
  'Z:\ai\models\unet'` (30 jobs), across three unrelated projects. `UnetLoaderGGUF`
  reads `Z:/ai/models/unet`; `CLIPTextEncode` reads `Z:/ai/models/text_encoders`. One
  failing drive, two error strings, depending on which node touches it first.
  facet-catalog was simply the only project queueing work when the drive first flaked.
- **Method note for both agents:** every t-068 RECHECK from 08-13 to 08-22 re-sampled
  `recentFailed` (last 25) and re-confirmed "still 100% facet-catalog". A last-25 window
  on a serially-draining queue will report homogeneity almost regardless of the truth.
  Pulling the *full* FAILED set (7 pages of `/api/art/queue?status=FAILED`) and grouping
  by `(day, projectSlug, signature)` took one script and immediately showed two
  signatures, three projects, and one shared drive path. Prefer the full set over the
  sample when the question is "what is the scope of this".
- **Tooling gap, now closed:** there was no supported way to resubmit an infra-caused
  backlog. `repair_failed_kindrobots_artjobs.py` is deliberately payload-scoped and
  correctly selected 0 of 420, printing all of them as "unhandled". The bare
  `reenqueue-failed` endpoint has no policy at all — aiming it at 420 ids while the host
  is down burns ~1250 render attempts and overwrites every original error string with
  the same one, destroying the diagnosis. Added
  `scripts/drain_failed_art_backlog.py`: classifies by failure cause, refuses to
  resubmit payload faults, and gates the drain behind a live canary batch that must
  actually render first.
- Verified live before writing any of this down: requeued 9511/9512/9513 as a canary.
  9511 was claimed by `Silas-PC` within a minute and reproduced WinError 1117 on its
  first attempt, then failed out at 3. So the 416 retryable jobs were deliberately left
  FAILED, with their error text intact.

**Suggested action:** Silas — the render box's `Z:` share is unreadable; remount it,
restart ComfyUI so `folder_paths` rebuilds its cached filename lists, then run
`python scripts/drain_failed_art_backlog.py --live`. It canaries first and aborts if the
drive is still bad, so it is safe to run before checking. Agents — when a failure
signature is used to scope an incident, confirm the scope against the full FAILED set,
not `recentFailed`.

## 2026-08-25 | Reviewer → Worker | system | critique
type: critique

**Subject:** The relay described a dead disk as a prompt problem, twice, and a human reading
its own logs reached the wrong conclusion. Error wording is a correctness surface.

**Detail:**
- Silas read the kr-relay log for the 2026-08-25 backlog and concluded "this really looks
  like we're sending bad prompts." That is the *correct* reading of what the relay wrote.
  It was wrong, and the relay's wording is why.
- Message 1: `ComfyUI POST /prompt failed at ... No accepted prompt for client ...
  appeared within 120.0s`. Leads with the prompt, ends with the prompt, and buries an
  `OSError` on `Z:\ai\models\unet` in a dict dump in between. The traceback ends at
  `class_inputs = obj_class.INPUT_TYPES()` — a classmethod taking no arguments, called to
  enumerate the models the box *has*, before ComfyUI compares any submitted value.
- Message 2, four hours later, same drive, new presentation: `ComfyUI has no matching file
  for: CLIPLoader.clip_name='qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors'`. That file is registered
  and rendered fine at 07:20Z the same morning. `folder_paths` had re-enumerated a
  half-readable share and returned a short list. The relay reported a working model as
  missing, in wording that points squarely at the payload.
- **Both were fixed at the source rather than worked around.**
  `host_fault_in_node_errors()` now reports an `OSError` inside `node_errors` as "ComfyUI
  cannot read its own model files", naming node and path. `unresolved_asset_error()` now
  reports how many files ComfyUI listed for the failing input — the count is the whole
  diagnosis, because a name absent from a healthy list is a misnaming and the same name
  absent from a list that has shrunk is a lost mount.
- **This also caught a real bug in my own tool.** `drain_failed_art_backlog.py` classified
  `payload-model-missing` as never-retryable, which is right for ArtJob 9181 (an invented
  filename from t-033) and wrong for these 30. It now cross-checks the named files against
  the Kind Robots Resource registry: registered file the box lost → retryable host fault;
  unregistered file → held back. Without that check the drain would have permanently
  stranded 30 good jobs, and I would have shipped it.

**Suggested action:** when a component reports someone else's fault, it owns saying so
plainly. "POST /prompt failed" for a disk error and "no matching file" for a file that
exists are both technically true and both actively misleading — they cost a human a wrong
diagnosis and nearly cost 30 jobs. Before shipping a fail-fast, read its message as
someone who will see it in a log at 3pm with no other context.

**Subject:** Unrecognized auto-start entry on the render box (Silas-PC), on the machine that

  expected entries (Steam, Discord, Docker, PM2, …), one that does not belong to any

  ```
  业余分开蓝色    REG_SZ    C:\Users\silasfelinus\AppData\Roaming\业余分开蓝色\业余分开蓝色.exe
  ```

- Not asserting this is malicious — it has not been examined. But the shape matches the
  common persistence pattern closely enough to warrant checking before anything else on
  that box is trusted: a CJK-named executable whose folder and filename are identical,
  living under `AppData\Roaming` (per-user, no admin needed to write), launched from the
  per-user Run key. The name reads as machine-generated rather than as a product name.
- Why it matters more than usual here. Silas-PC holds `KR_RELAY_TOKEN` (machine-user
  credentials against kindrobots.org), `KR_CIVITAI_TOKEN`, and — as of this session — a
  Credential Manager entry for the alexandria SMB shares. Anything running as that user
  inherits all of it, including write access to the array while the array has no
  redundancy left (disk4 emulated, disk13 at 1.09M errors).
- NOT claiming a connection to the disk incident. disk13's error count is far better
  explained by hardware; conflating the two would be guessing. Flagged as a separate
  finding that surfaced during the same investigation.

**Suggested action:** FOR SILAS — before rebooting or re-trusting the box, capture and check
rather than delete (deleting destroys the evidence and not necessarily the persistence):

```
Get-Item "$env:APPDATA\业余分开蓝色\业余分开蓝色.exe" | Select FullName,Length,CreationTime
Get-AuthenticodeSignature "$env:APPDATA\业余分开蓝色\业余分开蓝色.exe" | Select Status
Get-FileHash "$env:APPDATA\业余分开蓝色\业余分开蓝色.exe" -Algorithm SHA256
```

Put the SHA256 into VirusTotal. If it comes back clean and signed, it is someone's oddly
named utility and this entry can be closed. If it is unsigned, recently created, or flagged,
then `KR_RELAY_TOKEN` and `KR_CIVITAI_TOKEN` should be rotated and the Unraid password for
`silasfelinus` changed, since all three are reachable from that user account.

Per hard rule 8 this stays surfaced until Silas acknowledges it either way.

The `distribute-images` workflow's last real run (2026-08-24, run #10) had crashed on the first `cthulhuquarium-fish-*.webp` file it hit: `shutil.SameFileError` from a queue entry whose `image_path` was the `projects/process/` staging path itself (`target_repo: null`) — `resolve_abs_path()` returned the same path as the source file, and `shutil.copy2(src, dest)` doesn't accept `src == dest`. Everything alphabetically after that file (animation-manager, animation-studio, conductor-app, fauvism, tonalism) never got a chance to process.
- No session had noticed because subsequent commits adding more files to `projects/process/` were pushed with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the workflow's own "Loop safety" comment documents that such pushes don't trigger downstream workflows), so the crash was never even retried, let alone fixed.
- Fixed with a defensive same-file check that routes such an entry to `projects/process/unmatched/` instead of crashing the batch (conductor#2937), with a regression test that reproduces the exact `SameFileError` and confirms the rest of a mixed batch still lands. Verified by reverting the fix locally and confirming the new test fails identically, then triggered the workflow live via `workflow_dispatch` after merging and confirmed it completed successfully (no crash) — though by the time it ran, an unrelated scheduled `queue_missing_project_art.py` regeneration had already dropped the cthulhuquarium entries from the live queue, so the actual production run classified those files via the `RETAIN` (kind_robots slug-inspiration) path rather than exercising the new same-file guard directly. The guard is still real and tested against the exact crash shape from the historical failed run.
- Root cause of *why* `queue_missing_project_art.py` produced entries with `target_repo: null` and a self-referential `image_path` in the first place is still open — noted in the PR's kaizen section rather than guessed at.

**What was good:** didn't stop at "this crash predates me, not my problem" — traced it back to an actual reproducible historical failure (the Aug 24 job log) before writing a fix, rather than guessing at the cause from the symptom alone.

**Kaizen suggestion:** audit `queue_missing_project_art.py` for why it can emit `target_repo: null` + self-referential `image_path` entries — not filed as a new task this cycle since the immediate symptom (the crash) is fixed and the root cause needs someone to actually read that generator's logic, which is out of scope for a scheduled sweep that found it as a side effect of other work.

## 2026-08-27 | Agent (scheduled conductor run) | system | pattern

**Subject:** `git checkout main && git reset --hard origin/main` (a routine state-refresh done to pick up an unrelated just-merged PR) silently discarded an uncommitted edit this same session had made earlier in the same repo checkout, for a different, not-yet-committed task.

**Detail:**
- This session edited conductor's `projects/cthulhuquarium/data/economy.yaml` (adding a new `rare_events` section) as design research, uncommitted, before claiming `cthulhuquarium/t-016`. It then did substantial unrelated work in the kind_robots repo, merged that PR, and came back to the conductor repo to refresh local state with `git checkout main && git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main` -- a sequence this repo's own sessions run constantly and correctly for the *intended* purpose (discarding a stale local branch/HEAD after a remote merge). `reset --hard` did exactly what it's documented to do: it also silently wiped the still-uncommitted `economy.yaml` edit, which had nothing to do with the PR that had just merged.
- Caught immediately by grepping the file for the expected content right after the reset, rather than assuming it survived -- no data was actually lost since the edit was simple to redo from memory, but a more complex or long-running uncommitted edit could have been a real loss with no recovery path (unlike a committed-but-unpushed commit, which at least survives in reflog).
- This is a different flavor of the git-state-mutating hazard CLAUDE.md already documents at length (background-subagent races, HTTP 413 workarounds) -- those are about *concurrent* actors stepping on each other's state. This one is a *single* session stepping on its own earlier, unrelated, uncommitted work via a command that is completely correct for its stated purpose.

**Suggested action:** before running any `git reset --hard`/`git checkout -f`/similar in a repo this session has been actively editing, run `git status --porcelain` first and treat any dirty output as a stop sign -- commit it (even to a scratch branch) or explicitly confirm it's disposable before proceeding. Worth a line in AGENTS.md's git-safety section if this recurs; not filing a new task for it solo since it didn't cause any actual loss this time, but flagging here so the next session that hits it recognizes the pattern immediately rather than re-diagnosing from scratch.

in either one. (1) `refreshPool()` originally announced arrivals whenever `seenIds` was
non-empty, so raising the depth from 12 to 200 would have queued ~188 hours-old renders as
cut-to-front "new art". Window refreshes now never announce; only the head poll does. (2) The
`pendingArrivalCount` watcher fired once per decrement, so three renders finishing inside one
poll would have flashed past in three consecutive ticks; it now only interrupts on a 0 -> n
transition and lets the rest play at the natural interval. Both are the kind of thing a
component test wouldn't have caught either -- they needed reading the two callers together.

**Suggested action:** none blocking. Worth noting for a future session: the slideshow is
deliberately an overlay inside the admin-gated queue browser rather than its own route,
because AGENTS.md requires Silas's approval for a new top-level surface. If he wants to leave
it running on a second monitor without the dashboard behind it, that is a small follow-up --
a dedicated route plus the dashboard/tutorial registration and `Project.liveUrl` bookkeeping
AGENTS.md calls for -- and it needs his approval first.

## 2026-08-29 — a truncated error in a DB-less sandbox is not automatically a connection error

**Context:** kind-robots/t-077 shipped a home page redesign whose whole surface hangs off one
new endpoint, `/api/showcase/home`. It merged, and Silas's first load showed only the newsfeed
plus "The showcase couldn't be loaded just now" -- the endpoint 500'd on every request. Root
cause and fix are in kind-robots/t-079 (kind_robots#2188); this entry is about how it got past
review, which is the reusable half.

**What happened:** the build sandbox has no database, so a 500 from a new data endpoint read as
expected background noise. The first curl of the route actually returned:

```
Invalid `prisma.dream.findMany()` invocation:
{ where: { isActive: true, isPublic: true, ... } }
```

That is the *validation* error format, not a connection error -- Prisma renders the offending
arguments and names the bad field at the END of the message. It was truncated at 400 characters
during the session, the visible half looked like a connection failure, and it was not pursued.
A later probe returned a genuine pool timeout, which confirmed the wrong conclusion.

**The generalisable lesson, in two parts:**

1. **Prisma validates a query BEFORE it opens a connection.** So a sandbox with no database is
   NOT prevented from checking query shape -- it is one of the few things it can still check.
   Instantiating the generated client with a throwaway adapter and calling each query is
   enough: a valid query fails with `pool timeout: failed to retrieve a connection`, an invalid
   one fails with `Unknown field ... for select statement on model ...`, and the two are
   trivially distinguishable. Worth doing for any new endpoint that fans out over several
   models, especially one behind `Promise.all`, where a single bad query takes down all of them.

2. **Read the whole error before classifying it.** The distinguishing text was past the
   truncation point. "No database here, so of course it 500s" is a hypothesis that explains the
   symptom without being tested, and it suppressed the one signal that would have caught this
   before merge.

**What was good:** the endpoint's own error handling behaved correctly -- it returned a fixed
public message rather than forwarding the Prisma dump to the front page, and the page degraded
to its error note instead of breaking. The failure was diagnostic discipline, not resilience.

**Suggested action:** none filed as a task. The compile-time guard in kind_robots#2188 (a
`satisfies` intersection on the shared select constant) prevents this specific class from
recurring in that file, and a runtime query-shape verifier was considered and deliberately not
built: the only low-drift version would have to import the endpoint's own loaders, and a
verifier that re-declares the queries would drift from them and quietly stop testing anything.
Worth revisiting if a second endpoint of this shape appears.

## 2026-08-29 | Agent (Claude) | ops/home-server | ferngrotto reboot dropped the SMB mappings

**Subject:** Third share outage in five days, but the first one caused by the *render box*
rebooting rather than the NAS. Added a logon-time repair script for the case the existing
watchdog structurally cannot cover.

**Detail:**
- Live state at report time: `scripts/check_render_box.py` said DOWN — media origin answering
  HTTP 404, 1 stale RUNNING claim, 630 PENDING and nothing completing. Stalled, not idle.
- The 2026-08-25/26 work covers a NAS that goes away while this box stays up: `healthcheck.ps1`
  probes one path, remaps one letter from `KR_SHARE_UNC`, restarts ComfyUI on the down->up edge.
  None of that reaches a client reboot: a `schtasks /SC MINUTE` task made without `/RU` does not
  run at all until its user logs on; it repairs one of four mappings; and letters mapped by a
  service or a SYSTEM task land in a logon session nobody is sitting in, so no daemon can restore
  them on Silas's behalf.
- Since 2026-08-27 the pipeline itself is off drive letters (`KR_SHARE_ROOT` and
  `extra_model_paths.yaml` both on `//192.168.7.172/pc`), so a lost letter no longer stops a
  render. What still stops one is a missing `cmdkey` credential, which presents identically to a
  dead NAS and is per-user — the account pm2 runs as needs its own. That is now the documented
  first check after a reboot.
- Added `ops/home-server/restore-shares.ps1`: `-Save` snapshots the healthy letter->UNC table to
  a gitignored `shares.json` (and refuses to record a mapping it cannot read, so running it
  during an outage can't bake the outage into the config), `-Check` reports, default restores.
  Waits on TCP 445 before remapping (a logon trigger fires while the NIC is still negotiating),
  enumerates rather than trusting `Test-Path`, names any host without a stored credential, and
  restarts ComfyUI if it restored anything and can see the pm2 daemon.

**Honest limit:** none of this was executed against ferngrotto — no route to the box from this
sandbox. The script is unrun; PowerShell 5.1 has no linter here either, so it is reviewed-by-
reading only, kept ASCII-only per the existing `healthcheck.ps1` codepage note. First real
execution is `-Check` on the box.

**Then the diagnosis was wrong, twice, and the corrections are the valuable part.** Both errors
came from trusting this repo's own documentation over live evidence:

1. Asserted the outage was `Z:`-specific because Silas said "the others are fine." `net use`
   showed all four (V:/W:/Y:/Z:, all `\\192.168.7.172\...`) `Unavailable`. Should have asked for
   the listing before theorizing.
2. Asserted the model share was provably healthy, reasoning that kr-relay had claimed a job and
   its share gate enumerates the path before every claim. ArtJob 10258 then failed at 09:50 with
   `[WinError 3] ... 'Z:\'` — the relay was still on the drive letter, two days after this repo
   recorded the move to UNC as done, so its claim proved nothing. **Root cause of the drift:
   `pm2 resurrect` replays the env captured at the last `pm2 save`, so a `setx` made after that
   save never reaches the process and every reboot restores the stale env.** Fixed in the README
   along with the standing lesson: documentation of an intended state is not evidence of the
   deployed state.

**Resolved.** The fault was a stale SMB credential, not a mount: `cmdkey /list` showed entries
for both `192.168.7.172` and `alexandria` while every share answered `The user name or password
is incorrect`. Re-adding replaced the password and `dir \\192.168.7.172\pc\ai\models` listed all
60 directories, matching the 2026-08-26 audit. Two traps recorded in the README: a listed
credential is not a working credential, and `cmdkey /add` cannot write from a network logon
session at all (`CMDKEY: Credentials cannot be saved from this logon session` — Silas was in
Termius, the same session confusion as 2026-08-25). Also noted that the three shells disagree
about the same fault and only cmd is honest: cmd `The user name or password is incorrect`,
PowerShell `Cannot find path ... because it does not exist`, ComfyUI `no matching file for` a
model that is present.

**Suggested action:** Silas runs `-Save` once while the mappings are healthy — the script has
nothing to restore from until he does. Separately, kr-relay has no preflight against a ComfyUI
that is not yet listening (jobs 10255-10257 burned to FAILED at 3 attempts each during a boot
window, `WinError 10061`), which is the same shape as the share gate and worth the same
treatment. Not filed as a task yet — awaiting Silas.

## 2026-08-29 | Agent (Claude) | ops/home-server | remove A1111/Forge from the render box

**Subject:** Silas: "we should not have references to a1111 period. it's an old app, it's not used
at all." Removed it from everything that runs; left the historical record and one user-facing
kind_robots feature that is not the same thing.

**Detail:**
- Surfaced by the reboot recovery: `pm2 restart ecosystem.config.js` started `sd-webui` (and
  `kr-download`) because restarting an ecosystem file starts every app defined in it, not just
  the running ones. The subsequent `pm2 save` then froze a six-app list into `dump.pm2`, so every
  future boot would have brought A1111 up to hold VRAM ComfyUI wanted.
- Removed: the `sd-webui` pm2 app and `SD_DIR` (`ecosystem.config.js`), the `sd-webui` liveness
  target (`healthcheck.ps1`), `run_a1111`/`SD_URL`/the A1111 heartbeat (`relay_agent.py`), the
  A1111 branch in `relay_media_agent.py`, and every live instruction in `README.md` /
  `SELF-HOSTED-MEDIA.md` / `start-engines.bat`.
- `resolve_job_engine` now accepts COMFY only and rejects anything else with "this relay only
  drives ComfyUI". Deliberate reversal of the earlier "explicit A1111 jobs remain supported"
  decision: with the app gone those jobs could only time out against a dead port 7860, so failing
  fast with a real reason is strictly better. Test renamed to assert the rejection.
- **Found a latent bug while cutting:** `relay_media_agent.py` defaulted an unlabeled job to
  `A1111` (`job.get("engine") or "A1111"`) while `relay_agent.py` defaulted the same job to
  `COMFY`. Any job reaching the direct-media path without an explicit engine would have gone to
  A1111. Both now route through `relay.resolve_job_engine`.
- **Kept deliberately, flagged to Silas:** (1) the `"a1111": "krea2"` normalization in
  `consume_art_queue_core.py` -- that is data compatibility for yaml entries already on disk, and
  removing it converts a silent migration into a hard rejection; no live yaml uses it. (2)
  `docs/art-api.md` and the kind_robots A1111 server type -- `POST /api/art/generate` is a live,
  mana-gated endpoint where *users register their own* A1111 server, backed by a Prisma enum,
  stores, and UI. That is a product feature, not detritus on this box, and deleting it is a
  schema/migration decision. (3) Roadmap/CHANGELOG/LEARNING history, which is the record.

**Verification:** full suite `1378 passed, 1 skipped, 35 subtests` in 98s; `ecosystem.config.js`
loads under node and resolves to `comfyui, kr-relay, kr-download`. Not executed on ferngrotto --
Silas still needs `pm2 delete sd-webui && pm2 save` there to clear the app from the saved dump.

**What was good:** checking kind_robots before treating "no references period" as global -- the
same string names a dead local app and a live user-facing feature, and a blind sweep would have
broken the latter.

## 2026-08-29 | Agent (Claude, Silas-directed session) | art queue | resolution

**Subject:** The 22 FAILED ArtJobs were an infrastructure window, not bad payloads — but half of them were duplicates of art that already existed, and draining them would have overwritten it.

**Detail:**
- Silas: *"There are a bunch of art queue fails, can you look into them? It's possible it was a temporary comfy error, but make sure the formats for them are accurate."* Both halves of that turned out to be right, and the second one mattered more than expected.
- 22 FAILED, all `ruler-hooked`, all COMFY, all `attempts=3`, two error strings between them: eleven `[WinError 3] The system cannot find the path specified: 'Z:\'` (the self-hosted media share unmounted — `docs/self-hosted-media.md` maps it to `Z:\kindrobots\images`) and eleven `WinError 10061/10054/timed out` against `http://127.0.0.1:8188` (ComfyUI not accepting `POST /prompt`). Failure window 03:13Z–09:56Z. `drain_failed_art_backlog.py` classified all 22 retryable, correctly.
- **Formats verified rather than assumed.** Checked all 22 against kind_robots' own enqueue gates (`assertArtPromptContract`, `normalizeKindRobotsImagePath`) and against a structural diff with ArtJob 10276, a known-good DONE job from the same batch: no conditional instructions, no format vocabulary, no vague brand style, no text-exclusion pile, `cfg 1`/`steps 8` inside the krea2 distilled limits, every `imagePath` under `public/images/`, workflow graph identical node-for-node including link topology, same three registered models, node 3/4 text matching `promptString`/`negativePrompt`, latent and KSampler matching the payload. **0 of 22 had a format problem.** The decisive evidence is not the checker though: ArtJobs 10271–10276, same project and same graph, went DONE at 10:34–11:04Z — after the failure window — and the three canary requeues rendered on `attempts=1` with images live on the media origin.
- **The real finding.** Eleven of the 22 had already been rendered. A duplicate enqueue at 2026-08-27T11:46 re-queued a ruler-hooked batch whose originals completed 08-26 22:37–01:01 (ArtJobs 9921/9931–9939/9957 — the same 9935–9949 range `ruler-hooked/t-019`'s note names as the fish roster). All eleven target images return HTTP 200 today. The relay writes to the job's `imagePath`, so a blind drain would have re-rendered over eleven existing images at a different seed — replacing art that is sitting in a `needs-human` review gate with different art nobody asked for. `is_retryable()` answers whether the payload is sound; it does not answer whether the work is still wanted, and nothing in the drain path was asking the second question.
- Fixed in conductor#3196: the drain now HEADs the media origin per retryable job and holds back the ones already there, naming them in the report. Tri-state on purpose — only 2xx is `present`, 404/410 is `absent`, and a timeout or 5xx is `unknown` and stays in the drain, because an unreachable origin is not evidence an image exists and a wrongly-skipped job is a missing image nothing will queue again. `--include-rendered` re-rolls deliberately.
- Live outcome: dry run selected exactly the 11 duplicates; `--live --canary 3` rendered all three canaries (10260/10261/10262 DONE, `attempts=1`, images on media) and resubmitted the remaining 8. FAILED went 22 → 11, and the 11 left are the already-rendered duplicates.
- The duplicate-enqueue *cause* is already fixed: `conductor/t-133` (`has_unresolved_submission`, 2026-08-28) and `t-136` both closed, one day after these rows were created. These eleven are residue from before that guard, not a live leak.

**What was good:** treating "make sure the formats are accurate" as a claim to test rather than a box to tick. Replicating the enqueue contract against the live payloads and structurally diffing them against a known-good job from the same batch is what made "the payloads are fine, the host was down" a verified statement instead of a plausible one — and the media-existence check that fell out of the same pass is what caught the eleven that would have been silently re-rendered over.

**Suggested action:** Close out the 11 remaining FAILED rows with `POST /api/art/queue/cancel-failed` and a reason naming the DONE job that superseded each (10124→9931, 10125→9932, 10126→9933, 10127→9934, 10128→9935, 10129→9936, 10130→9937, 10131→9938, 10132→9939, 10154→9957, 10114→9921). Left undone here because cancelling production rows is Silas's call, not a drain script's. Until then the FAILED count reads 11 for work that is finished.

## 2026-08-30 | Agent (Claude, Silas-directed session) | art queue | correction + resolution

**Subject:** Correcting the previous entry — the eleven "already-rendered duplicates" were a deliberate re-render with a corrected prompt, and the seed was never random in the first place.

**Detail:**
- Silas asked a checking question about the previous entry: *"we are always randomizing the seed (-1) when we submit, yes? So even if a duplicate happened, it would not be identical?"* Verifying it rather than agreeing turned up two things I had wrong.
- **The seed was deterministic, not random.** `consume_art_queue.entry_to_job` replaced any unset or `-1` seed on a COMFY workflow lane with `stable_retry_seed()`: SHA-256 over `{id, image_path, project, prompt, engine}`. Same request identity, same seed, every submission. The reason was deduplication — `ArtJob.attemptFingerprint` (kind_robots `server/utils/artJobProvenance.ts`) hashes the whole payload including the baked workflow seed, so a stable seed is what makes the enqueue endpoint's dedupe fire on a repeat. My previous entry's phrase "at a different seed, and therefore a different picture" was right about the outcome and wrong about the mechanism, which is exactly the kind of detail that should not be asserted without reading the code.
- **The eleven were not duplicates.** All eleven pairs carry byte-identical subject text and a rewritten style block: the 08-26 originals name five franchises verbatim (`in the spirit of Monkey Island, Ralph Bakshi, Treasure Planet, Steven Universe, and She-Ra`) and pile four text negations (`no lettering anywhere, no collage, no contact sheet, no border`); the 08-27 jobs replace both. That is why their seeds differ — the prompt is an input to the seed hash, so a prompt edit re-rolls it. The rationale is documented at `scripts/build_ruler_hooked_art_queue.py:105-148` and both halves are real defects: `nix-pearl` + "Steven Universe" returned a direct likeness of that show's Pearl (an IP failure, not just a quality one), and krea2 at cfg 1 never applies a negative prompt, so `no lettering anywhere` put "lettering" into POSITIVE conditioning on a text-specialist model — `smugglers-map` came back as a scroll of garbled pseudo-writing trying to spell out its own prompt.
- So the images live on media were the defective-prompt renders, and the eleven FAILED rows were the fix that died in the outage. Cancelling them — which is what the previous entry recommended, and what Silas had approved on the strength of that recommendation — would have permanently discarded the correction and left the IP-leaking renders in place, including the fish designs sitting in `ruler-hooked/t-019`'s approval gate. Rerun with `--include-rendered` instead, on Silas's instruction once the real shape was clear.
- **Seed policy changed.** Silas, 2026-08-30: *"we do not want that infrastructure choice to set deterministic seeds. I see no reason to do it that way. If we resubmit the same prompt, we should always get a random seed."* `stable_retry_seed`/`retry_seed_identity`/`uses_specialized_attempt_recovery` are removed; every lane now falls through to `_core.resolve_seed`, which picks a fresh in-range random seed unless the entry names one. An explicit non-negative seed stays authoritative, so reproducing a specific render is still possible by asking for it. The old behavior meant a prompt could only ever yield one picture — there was no way to re-roll a bad render without editing the prompt, which is backwards for an art pipeline.
- Dedup is not lost with it: `consume_art_requests.has_unresolved_submission` (conductor/t-133, with t-136's release condition) blocks re-submission while the row's ArtJob is still in flight and keys on the recorded job id, not on payload bytes. What is lost is the `attemptFingerprint` backstop at the API — worth knowing if duplicate enqueues ever reappear.

**What was good:** Silas's question was a check on a detail I had asserted rather than verified, and taking it as a claim to test instead of a point to concede is what surfaced the restyle. The previous entry's confident "duplicates" framing had already been acted on once.

**Suggested action:** The `already-rendered` guard added in conductor#3196 stops a blind overwrite and reports what it held back, which is right — but it labels every held-back job the same way regardless of whether the queued prompt matches the one that produced the existing image. Comparing the queued `promptString` against the rendered job's would separate "duplicate, skip it" from "deliberate re-render, this is the fix" — the exact distinction that was missed here. Worth doing before the next backlog drain.

## 2026-09-01 | Agent (Claude, scheduled conductor run) | rainbow-butterflies/t-035 | security-flag

type: security-flag

**Subject:** kind_robots PR #2285 (untracked by any roadmap task) adds a new first-party BFF delegation auth mechanism for Rainbow with a real privilege-escalation gap; not merged.

**Detail:**
- Session-start sweep found kind_robots#2285 ("Add first-party BFF delegation for Rainbow") already open, authored outside the normal Conductor claim flow (no roadmap task referenced it anywhere across `projects/*/roadmap.yaml`). It adds a 7-day non-admin JWT ("first-party delegation") issuable via authorization-code exchange, direct Google exchange, or a brand-new password-based endpoint (`server/api/auth/first-party/password.post.ts`), letting Rainbow act as a Kind Robots user without holding a normal JWT/API key.
- Delegated a focused security review (GitHub MCP, read-only) rather than reviewing inline given the stakes. It found `server/utils/authGuard.ts`'s `requireHumanApiUser` — the guard meant to keep credential-management endpoints (`server/api/agent-credentials/**`, `server/api/agent-profiles/**`) reachable only by a "real, fully-authenticated user" (its own now-deleted doc-comment's words) — blocks `kind === 'agent-credential'` but never got updated to also block the new `kind === 'first-party-delegation'`. The PR's own diff touches this exact function and deletes that doc-comment without honoring it. Net effect: a delegation token obtained from the new password endpoint can mint itself new, independently-scoped, longer-lived `AgentCredential`s — a self-escalation path past its own 7-day window. The PR's new contract test (`tests/contracts/verifyFirstPartyDelegation.ts`) never asserts anything about `requireHumanApiUser`, so CI didn't catch it.
- Also flagged, non-blocking design points for Silas: the password endpoint has no rate limiting (a second unthrottled credential-testing surface, matching the existing gap on `login.post.ts`); `client_id` carries no secret in the password/exchange flows, so it authenticates nothing on its own; delegation tokens are stateless JWTs with no DB row/scopes/revocation, unlike the established `agentCredentials.ts` pattern — a compromised token is unrevocable for its full 7-day life.
- Posted the finding directly on kind_robots#2285 (issue comment; could not use a formal REQUEST_CHANGES review since the PR and this session share the same GitHub identity). Did **not** merge. Filed `rainbow-butterflies/t-035` (`status: needs-human`, `gate_human: true`, `security_flag: true`) with a FOR SILAS note naming the exact fix needed before merge and the three design points to decide.

**Suggested action:** Silas reviews kind_robots#2285 and `rainbow-butterflies/t-035`; have the `requireHumanApiUser` gap fixed (on the PR or a follow-up) before it merges, and decide the rate-limiting/client-secret/revocation questions. No other agent should merge #2285 until this task is resolved.

## 2026-09-02 | Agent (Claude, Silas-directed session) | art-job requeue audit | resolution

**Subject:** Silas asked whether the art-job requeue error reported as fixed actually was, and to kill any redundant art jobs. The reported fix (conductor#3443, t-142) is real and verified working — but it was only half the outage. A second, unreported and still-live bug had wiped conductor's entire art queue file 15 minutes before the session started, and 1,913 redundant ArtJobs were sitting PENDING against a corpus that is 100% rendered.

**Detail:**
- **Verified the reported fix.** Re-ran `queue_mandarin_tutor_art.queue_batch()` against the live v2 manifest with `append_request_blocks`/`write_snapshot` stubbed out (read-only, no repo mutation): `already_rendered: 577, probe_unknown: 0, missing: 0, queued: 0`. The live-media HEAD dedup t-142 added does exactly what it claims. Independently, `audit_mandarin_illustration_coverage.py --fetch` reports 577/577 rendered, 0 absent, 0 unknown.
- **t-142's note is incomplete and worth correcting in the record.** It says the 577-card re-stage was "caught before commit, reverted, never pushed." That is true of the manual audit session — but the scheduled `auto-art-generate` lane committed the same re-stage on its own: conductor `f650b07` (2026-09-02T04:55Z) added 10,973 lines of exactly those rows, and ArtJob id runs 16335-16690, 16913-17268, 17270-17846, 17848-18424 are four full-corpus submissions across 09-01 22h/23h and 09-02 04h. The duplicates were real and live, not hypothetical. Filed as conductor/t-143.
- **The bug nobody had noticed.** `f650b07` pushed `projects/art-prompts.yaml` to 1,424,189 bytes. The GitHub Contents API only inlines a body up to 1MB; past that it still answers 200 with the real sha and size, but `content` is `""` and `encoding` is `"none"`. kind_robots' `art-request.post.ts` decoded that unconditionally, so the next missing-image request read the queue as an **empty file**, found no duplicate to skip, and PUT a one-entry file over it — with the sha GitHub had just handed back, which GitHub accepted because the read was *current*, just bodiless. That is conductor `0e671cd`: **-11,014 lines**, 577 Mandarin rows and three in-flight missing-image requests gone in one write, and the wiped `rainbow-butterflies-icon` request re-enqueued as a fourth duplicate job for a target that already had three pending.
- **How it was pinned rather than guessed.** `appendRequest()` cannot drop content in any of its branches, and the PUT's sha was accepted, so the read was neither stale nor rejected — the only input that yields a one-entry file is `current === ""`. Blob size 1,424,189 > 1,048,576 supplies the reason.
- **Blast radius was wider than art-prompts.yaml.** `conductor-github.ts`'s `conductorGet()` had the identical blind decode and backs `task-action`, `overrides`, `pitch-vote`, `project-state`, `inbox` and the coloring-book writers — all read-modify-write. `TALKBACK.md` (this file) is already 2.9MB and `LEARNING.yaml` is 630KB; the next roadmap to cross 1MB would have been overwritten the same way.
- **Fixed** in silasfelinus/kind_robots#2320: new `server/utils/githubFileContents.ts` — `readGithubFile()` falls back to the Git Blobs API (base64 to 100MB) and **throws** rather than returning `""` for a file GitHub reports as non-empty; `githubPathExists()` keeps existence probes body-free; both call sites route through it; and the writer now asserts an append-only invariant (new exported `requestBlockIds`) before committing, so a write that would drop an existing request id fails loudly. New contract test wired into `contract-tests.yml`.
- **Killed the redundant jobs.** Verified redundancy first rather than inferring it from duplicate counts: HEAD-probed all 577 distinct mandarin v2 imagePaths against the media origin, 577/577 present, and counted only an authoritative 2xx as present so an origin hiccup could not widen the cancel set. Cancelled 1,913 PENDING jobs (1,909 mandarin + the four older `rainbow-butterflies-icon` duplicates), 1913/1913 succeeded. Queue went 1917 → 4 PENDING: exactly one job per genuinely-missing conductor project image. CANCELLED is reversible via the reenqueue route.
- **Restored what the wipe deleted.** Recovered the three deleted request rows from blob `38e70ea` and recorded `last_art_job_id: 18429` on the surviving icon row, so all four rows map 1:1 onto the four surviving PENDING jobs. Confirmed this cannot cause a re-submission: a dry run of `consume_art_requests.py` reports "No pending requests — nothing to do", because t-133/t-136's `has_unresolved_submission()` guard fires on each row's live job id. Full conductor suite green afterwards: 1553 passed, 1 skipped, 35 subtests.

**What was good:** not stopping at "the reported fix works." The fix did work, and confirming that took ten minutes — but the live queue still held 1,917 pending jobs, and that number is what led to `0e671cd`. A verification that had only re-run the fixed script and reported "clean" would have left a queue-destroying bug live in production and 1,909 redundant renders queued against a finished corpus.

**What to improve:** nothing in this repo caught the wipe. `0e671cd` is an 11,014-line deletion of a queue file committed by an automated writer, and no check, alert, or digest line flagged it — it was found by reading the git log while chasing something else. Worth a standing guard on the conductor side too, not only the writer's own new invariant: a check that flags any single commit deleting a large fraction of `art-prompts.yaml` or a `roadmap.yaml`.

**Kaizen task:** conductor/t-143 (root cause + fix, PR open) and conductor/t-144 (queue cleanup + row restore, done), both filed this session.

## 2026-09-04 | Reviewer (Claude, Silas-directed) | conductor + kind_robots | API-credit leak audit

**Subject:** Silas asked where his Anthropic API credits were going. The Conductor Agent Routine (hourly, Max plan) was NOT the spender -- its sessions carry no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. The credits went to (1) `hourly-conductor.yml` and `daily-digest.yml`, which handed the key to model-authored steps that duplicate work the Max sessions already do, and (2) kind_robots text routes, where a request that waived its mana charge via `useOwnResource: true` (or a public non-official Server) but attached no key fell through to the SITE's Anthropic/OpenAI key -- free to the caller, billed to Silas. Agents holding `KR_API_TOKEN` reached the same key through that server path.

**Decision:** keep the secret (Silas: *"I want them to have the option of the access, so I'm not removing the token"*), kill the leaks. Conductor: both scheduled workflows now grant the key only behind a `spend_api_credits` `workflow_dispatch` input; `author_dream_proposal.py` exits 0 without a key; sessions own the docket (CLAUDE.md step 7, one proposal per session when below the 5-day buffer); `test_no_unreviewed_model_spend.py` enforces the gate on every `schedule:` workflow. kind_robots: `manaGate` records `freeReason` and derives `siteKeyAllowed`; all seven cloud text routes resolve keys through `resolveGatedProviderKey`, which returns 402 instead of using the site key for an own-resource/free-server request. Admin, server-key, and FAMILY callers keep site-key access.

**Detail:**
- Ruled out: kind_robots has no scheduled tasks or uptime probes touching Anthropic; comment backfill defaults to an OpenAI model; Kapowarr has no Anthropic references; no workflow uses claude-code-action.
- Not done: no usage log per route yet. `gate.commit()` already accepts `providerCostUsd`; a follow-up could record actual provider spend so the digest can report it by route.

**What to improve:** the spend guard only ever audited workflow files. Spend that arrives through another service (kind_robots) on a token the session already holds is invisible to it -- the kind_robots-side policy module is the guard for that path now.

**Kaizen task:** none filed; the follow-up above is offered to Silas here rather than queued.

## 2026-09-05 | Agent (Claude, Silas-directed session) | dream-cycle/t-006 | production repair + three fixes

**Subject:** Silas asked to merge kind_robots#2414, run the bulk Krea semantic repair in apply mode for Facet/Character/Bot/Dream/Scenario/Reward, resubmit every tainted contextual Krea job, and promote the new outputs over the old art. #2414 was already merged on arrival. The production DB host is tailnet-only (every Prisma call from the sandbox dies as a 10s `active=0 idle=0` pool timeout, the `stored-art-paths.yml` comment describes exactly this), so the repair had to run as a GitHub Actions job behind the Tailscale step.

**Decision:** merged kind_robots#2424 (dispatch-only `krea-semantic-art-repair.yml`), #2426, #2428, #2429 (three validate-before-write aborts, each root-caused and fixed); ran the entity write (run 33978824187) and the Facet write (run 33981806514).

**Detail:**
- Dry run first (run 33977834661): entity scan 3482 jobs, 2138 replacements planned, 1057 legacy Facet jobs deferred to the Facet repair; Facet scan 992 v2/v3 targets. Checked the rewrite on real prompts locally before writing: for the daily-dream prompts the only change is the text-exclusion tail (`unmarked surfaces, free of text` -> `clean surfaces`); older jobs lose the `Name:`/`Species:` label blocks.
- Entity write: 2138 semantic `NEW_OUTPUT` replacements (ArtJob 18480-20617), 1 tainted pending job cancelled (18479), 1 superseded output preserved, 0 rewrite failures. Promotion needs no separate step: `applyEntityArtCompletion` moves the slot FK to the new ArtImage and links the prior render into EntityArtImage history. Verified on the first 16 replacements as they rendered (9 DONE, 9 promoted, 0 failed); the old image keeps a stale `entity:...:current:` path tag, which is storage placement, not primary status.
- Facet write aborted three times, every time inside the #2414 pass-3 validate-before-write guard with nothing mutated and the catalog lock released. (1) #2426: `LEGACY_GENERATED_IDENTITY` used one character class excluding both quote styles, so ten wrapper prompts whose titles contain straight quotes (`Carries a candle everywhere "just in case."`) read as curated and hit the contextual-wrapper rule. (2) #2428: `rewriteKreaWorkflowPositivePrompt` folded curly quotes in the `_meta.request_prompt` provenance copy while `normalizeArtPrompt` only collapses whitespace, so any prompt containing ’ “ ” failed "workflow prompt does not match" -- 22 Facet titles here, and reproduced for an API-shaped prompt, i.e. `/api/art/enqueue` had been refusing user-typed smart quotes since #2414 landed. (3) #2429: 28 Facets carry a seed-time `FacetProfile.metadata.artworkPrompt` (`Kind Robots premium Builder card illustration for Dream Types: Art. ...`) that the semantic scrubber does not recognize; the identity builder appended it verbatim and the format-vocabulary rule rejected `card illustration`. A metadata prompt is now used only if it names no app and passes the Krea contract on its own.
- Facet write result: 998 jobs (ArtJob 20618-21615: 992 v2/v3 resubmissions at priority 50, 6 coverage at -10), 3 superseded outputs preserved, 61 repair targets held behind catalog blockers (68 blocked entries: `sentence-title`, `setting-shaped-genre`), legacy `Facet.artPrompt` wrappers rewritten to semantic identity prompts (API-verified on Aardvark and Pallas's Cat).
- Each fix was proved against the whole live catalog before pushing: pulled all 1617 active Facets through the API and ran `buildFacetArtPayload` for all four variants locally (22 -> 28 -> 0 failures across the three passes). The dry run now builds payloads too, so it exercises the same contract as the write.
- Queue after both writes: 3126 pending, 0 failed, 0 stale running. The render box completes roughly 8-12 Krea jobs an hour, so the drain takes days. Replacements inherit their source priority (daily-dream sources at 200), so tomorrow's dream art queues behind today's 200-tier replacements. Added `scripts/verify_krea_repair_promotion.py` (defaults to both ranges, samples via the KR API, exit 1 on a DONE-but-unpromoted or failed job) for later sessions to report progress.
- End state: `main` clean on both repos, all four kind_robots PR branches auto-deleted on merge; `dream-cycle/t-006` note and `implementation_pr` updated.

**What was good:** treating each write abort as a fresh root-cause rather than a retry -- the second one turned out to be a shared-path regression from #2414 that had nothing to do with Facets and would have kept refusing real user prompts.

**What to improve:** the Facet dry run passed twice while the write was doomed, because (until #2426) dry-run skipped payload construction and my first local probe passed metadata as an object where the script expects a JSON string, hiding the third failure. A dry run that does not build exactly what the write builds is not a dry run.

**Kaizen task:** none filed -- the queue-drain check is the `verify_krea_repair_promotion.py` script plus `check_live_facet_coverage.py` in the existing session sweep; a task would only restate the t-006 note.

## 2026-09-05 | Reviewer (Claude, Silas-directed) | conductor + kind_robots | Alexandria container-log triage, day one

**Subject:** Silas asked whether the fresh scoopspress errors in the first daily container-log digest were caused by the WordPress files removed from Conductor the day before (conductor/t-106, PRs #3583 and #3604). They were not. Both scoopspress signatures predate the deletions, and nothing on Alexandria ever served from the Conductor copy.

**Detail:**
- scoopspress `PHP Warning: Undefined variable $enable_postal_code in ...class.cf7sa.front.action.php on line 90` (14 hits today): a bug in the live site's own copy of the "Accept Stripe Payments using Contact Form 7" plugin (v3.3). The variable is assigned only inside the per-form loop, so any page load without a Stripe-enabled form reads it undefined. The 2026-09-04 digest already carried the same warning stamped `Thu Sep 03 08:17` -- eleven hours before #3583 merged -- so it was firing before anything was deleted. The Conductor tree was a reference copy (`projects/humboldt-scoop/README.md`: *"we have different versions hosted as actual unraid containers"*); `deploy-unraid.sh` pulls kind_robots only and never touched Conductor. Fix is on the WordPress side: update or replace the plugin, or set `enable_postal_code` on each Stripe form.
- scoopspress `script '/var/www/html/phpinfo.php' not found or unable to stat` (16 hits, client 35.220.201.92): an internet scanner probing for a leaked phpinfo page; the site correctly has none. Background noise on any public WordPress host.
- Why they showed as `new` at all: `container_log_triage.py`'s skeleton rules only knew numeric timestamps. Apache's `[Sat Sep 05 05:35:07 2026]` collapsed to `[sat sep <num> <ts> <num>]` with the WEEKDAY intact, so the same warning earned a fresh fingerprint each day (Thu/Fri fingerprints sit in yesterday's `top`, Sat in today's `new`) and could never build a baseline or be muted once. Fixed in kind_robots: word-form timestamp rules (Apache error log, CLF access log, syslog) run ahead of the numeric ones, with regression tests; the two undefined-variable rows (with/without `referer`) also merge into one. Expect scoopspress to drop out of `new` tomorrow and appear as a standing signature instead.
- Rest of the digest (22 new across 43 containers): prowlarr Newznab metadata warnings, flaresolverr queue depth, bazarr subtitle-save errors, sab encrypted-RAR pause, netdata disk-space alert, audiobookshelf socket timeouts and one unreadable podcast file. Routine. The 4000-hit ownfoil verification loop from yesterday's review is still the volume leader (now on a Pokémon NSP rather than The Sinking City) and still wants the file removed from its library.

**What to improve:** the first two days of a baseline-diff tool are exactly when a normalization gap looks like a real incident. Worth reading each `new` row's skeleton for leftover natural-language tokens (weekday, month) before believing it.

**Kaizen task:** none filed; the fix landed directly.

## 2026-09-06 | Agent (Claude, Silas-directed session) | kind-robots (creation burst: The Shellback Reaches) | pattern

**Subject:** Silas asked for the umbrella: *"how about a dream vibe to unite everything; something for a made up area in a D&D world, with the monastery as centerpiece, plus it's giant tortoises, and then a scenario where tom tomtum has to save the monastery from attack from brigades [brigands]. Everything tied together as appropriate."*

**Decision:** built PITCH Dream 5733 (The Shellback Reaches, slug `shellback-reaches`, HYBRID) with PitchSheet 1569, DreamRelation 331 (5733 CONTAINS location 5732), and Scenario 2213 (The Night the Long Quiet Broke, cast with 3332 + 3333, linked to both Dreams). World membership verified live: 2 characters, 2 rewards, 1 scenario. ArtJobs 21622/21623 at priority 300.

**Detail:**
- `creation_burst.py` gained a `world:` block — the umbrella PITCH Dream, with its own slug, a PitchSheet with a highlight trio, a CONTAINS relation to every location, and every character/reward/scenario as its members.
- **Membership is written from the world card, not onto each row.** Dream PATCH sets `characterIds`/`rewardIds`/`scenarioIds`, which is lossless here because the world card is bundle-owned and its members are exactly the bundle's rows. The alternative — PATCHing each Character — was rejected: Character PATCH's own `dreamIds` is also a `set:`, and the Character GET-by-id does not return its Dreams, so there is no safe way to read the current list first. Patching from the row side would silently drop any unrelated Dream a Character belongs to. This is also what back-linked the four rows built in earlier runs.
- `POST /api/dream-relations` is an upsert on `(fromDreamId, toDreamId, relationType)`, so re-running never duplicates a relation. No extra idempotency bookkeeping needed.
- Fixed a latent rollback bug found while wiring the sheet: `kr_create` recorded the create path as the delete path, but a PitchSheet is created at `POST /api/sheets/by-dream/{dreamId}` and deleted at `DELETE /api/sheets/{id}`. A failed build after the sheet landed would have built a nonsense URL and stranded it. `kr_create` now takes `delete_base` (same case `build_dream_records._delete_base` documents), with a test.
- The bundle's `title:`/`vibe:` now name the region rather than Tom, because those two strings are the world context in every FUTURE art prompt. The `slug:` deliberately stays `tom-tomtum` — it keys the already-staged art request ids, and changing it would re-stage art for rows that already have it.
- Tests: 6 new cases (world optional/validated, world prompt, world body slug fallback, sheet highlights, delete_base). Full suite 1744 passed.

**Suggested action:** none. The set is now reachable from one card: the world card lists everyone, contains the monastery, and the scenario names all three.
